items.title: Une rose pour Fatma ( par Elhadji Ibrahima THIAM)
items.description: Octobre rose. Une couleur chatoyante, gaie, pour parler d’une sombre réalité. D’une terrible maladie dont les souffrances, pour ceux qui la vivent comme pour leurs proches, sont incommensurables. Sa seule évocation suffit à faire frémir, tant le cancer, tous types confondus, fait peur. Il est peu de familles qui n’en aient pas éprouvé les ravages. Cette maladie a ceci de morbide qu’elle ruine avant de tuer. Tout le monde le sait. Et pourtant, tout le monde s’accroche, lutte, livre un combat dont l’issue semble parfois presque écrite d’avance. Comme si l’on se battait contre une fatalité. Au Sénégal, le cancer du sein entraîne plus de 1.300 décès par an, pour environ 2.220 nouveaux cas recensés annuellement, selon les chiffres avancés. Un constat glaçant, qui donne la mesure du fléau. Mais c’est aussi dans la nature humaine de s’accrocher au moindre espoir lorsque la vie semble nous échapper peu à peu. Alors, le meilleur rempart reste la prévention. Encore faut-il qu’elle soit accessible, comprise et pratiquée. Car elle ne garantit pas d’échapper à la maladie, surtout lorsque celle-ci frappe sans prévenir. Et parler de prévention, c’est aussi parler de sensibilisation. Au Sénégal, octobre rose est devenu un rendez-vous important, presque incontournable. Si cette campagne a fini par s’inscrire dans l’agenda national, on le doit certainement à la détermination de certaines figures. Parmi elles, la Dr Fatma Guenoune, spécialiste des pathologies cervico-vaginales et présidente de la Ligue sénégalaise contre le cancer (Lisca) depuis une douzaine d’années. Une brave dame qui s’est tellement investie dans le combat contre les cancers féminins qu’elle a fini par en être le porte-flambeau. Grâce à elle, des milliers de femmes ont sans doute pu être prises en charge, soignées, sauvées, ou ont gagné de précieuses années de vie. Et, ironie du sort, aujourd’hui, c’est elle que le cancer a happée. Cruel destin. Au lieu de s’apitoyer sur son sort, Fatma Guenoune a choisi de faire face. Avec un courage remarquable, elle a décidé de révéler elle-même sa maladie. Pas en pleurnichant, pas en geignant, mais en assumant cette nouvelle réalité avec le sourire. Ce sourire qui, depuis une quarantaine d’années, accueillait les femmes malades venues frapper à sa porte, chercher une écoute, un soutien, une solution, parfois simplement une raison de continuer à espérer. Dans les médias, Fatma Guenoune est allée raconter son histoire. Celle d’une combattante devenue, à son tour, une patiente. Pas pour quémander la pitié, encore moins pour susciter une compassion facile. Mais pour témoigner. Pour montrer à toutes ces femmes que le cancer n’enlève ni la dignité ni le courage, et qu’il est possible de regarder la maladie en face sans renoncer à soi-même. Son témoignage bouleverse parce qu’il renverse les rôles. Celle qui rassurait les autres a besoin, à son tour, d’être entourée. Celle qui incarnait l’espoir pour tant de femmes se retrouve confrontée à ses propres incertitudes. Mais elle n’a pas baissé les bras. Elle parle, elle témoigne, elle expose sa vulnérabilité, et ce faisant, elle poursuit son combat. En choisissant de rendre sa maladie publique, Fatma Guenoune prolonge, autrement, le travail qu’elle mène depuis des décennies. Son histoire devient un message adressé à toutes les femmes : ne pas attendre, se faire dépister, consulter, écouter son corps. Et ne jamais laisser la peur empêcher de chercher de l’aide. En ce mois d’Octobre, une rose pour Fatma. Pas une rose de circonstance, offerte le temps d’une campagne avant d’être oubliée. Une rose de gratitude, de respect et de solidarité. Celle qui ne fane pas : pour toutes ces années consacrées aux autres ; pour les femmes qu’elle a accompagnées. Et pour cette leçon de courage qu’elle nous donne aujourd’hui, au moment même où elle en a, elle aussi, le plus besoin. Bon rétablissement, Dr Guenoune. Le Sénégal vous doit bien plus qu’une rose. elhadjibrahima.thiam@lesoleil.sn

items.title: SOGUIPAL bénéficie d’un financement de 5 millions d’euros de Proparco pour porter la production de Best Yaourt à 15 tonnes par jour
items.description: L’industrie agroalimentaire guinéenne poursuit son développement. À Sanoyah, dans les installations de la Société Guinéenne de Produits Alimentaires (SOGUIPAL), les visiteurs ont pu découvrir les équipements et les capacités de production de l’entreprise, qui commercialise notamment la marque Best Yaourt. Au cœur de cette visite, un investissement destiné à renforcer la production locale et à répondre davantage aux besoins du marché guinéen. Pour accompagner cette expansion, Proparco a accordé un financement de 5 millions d’euros à l’entreprise, dans le cadre d’un programme d’investissement de 7,2 millions d’euros. L’objectif est de faire passer la capacité de production de l’unité de yaourt de 9 à 15 tonnes par jour, soit une augmentation d’environ 67 %, avec la création annoncée de 30 emplois directs. Autour du PDG-fondateur de SOGUIPAL, Ibrahima Diallo, plusieurs personnalités ont pris part à cette visite, notamment l’ambassadeur de France en Guinée, Luc Briard, le directeur régional Afrique de l’Ouest de Proparco, Sadio Dicko, le chef de cabinet du ministère de l’Industrie et du Commerce et le secrétaire général du ministère du Plan et de la Coopération internationale. Des représentants d’entreprises françaises, des responsables institutionnels et des employés de l’usine étaient également présents. Ibrahima Diallo salue un climat favorable à l’investissement Pour Ibrahima Diallo, PDG-fondateur de SOGUIPAL, cette augmentation des capacités de production témoigne de la volonté de son entreprise de poursuivre son développement dans un environnement qu’il juge favorable à l’investissement. « C'est le Président qui nous donne confiance en notre pays. C'est une personne visionnaire. Quand on fait un investissement, c'est le Président qui nous permet de faire l'investissement. Après, ça tombe bien. Il est ambitieux pour le développement de notre pays. Pour maintenir notre capacité de production, on s'organise comme ça. Avant, on faisait 9 tonnes par jour. Maintenant, on fait 15 tonnes par jour. On a créé des points de vente pour toutes les régions », a-t-il déclaré. Au-delà de l’augmentation des volumes, le développement du réseau de distribution constitue un autre enjeu pour l’entreprise, qui entend rendre ses produits disponibles dans les différentes régions du pays. Filiale du groupe CCG, SOGUIPAL développe plusieurs marques dans le secteur agroalimentaire. Outre Best Yaourt, son portefeuille comprend notamment Best Milk, Best Tomato, Best Mayo et Jadida. Proparco mise sur la production locale et l’emploi Pour Sadio Dicko, directeur régional Afrique de l’Ouest de Proparco, ce financement doit permettre à l’entreprise de franchir un nouveau cap grâce à l’installation de nouveaux équipements industriels. « Ce que nous avons vu aujourd'hui, cet après-midi, c'est très concrètement ce que PROPARCO finance. De nouveaux équipements qui vont faire passer la capacité de l'unité de yaourt de 9 à 15 tonnes par jour, et créer une trentaine d’emplois. Les équipements en grande partie français, cela a été dit, TECNAL pour ne pas les citer pour la production, et ERCA pour le conditionnement au service d'une production guinéenne », a-t-il expliqué. Le responsable de Proparco a également insisté sur les enjeux liés à la consommation de produits laitiers en Guinée, où les importations occupent encore une place importante. « Ce projet, il a du sens, il a beaucoup de sens, car la Guinée importe encore l'essentiel des produits laitiers qu'elle consomme. Produire ici, c'est proposer aux familles un produit plus frais, de qualité et accessible. C'est créer aussi de la valeur et des emplois en Guinée », a-t-il souligné. L’accompagnement ne se limite pas au financement. Le projet bénéficie également d’un appui technique dans les domaines de la qualité, de l’hygiène, de la sécurité et de l’environnement. Selon Sadio Dicko, cette opération constitue le premier projet guinéen de l’approche de Proparco consacrée à la croissance, dans le cadre de l’initiative FARM, portée par le président français Emmanuel Macron. Présent lors de la visite, l’ambassadeur de France en Guinée, Luc Briard, a salué un partenariat qu’il considère comme une illustration concrète de la coopération économique entre les deux pays. « Quel honneur d'être là ce matin, ce après-midi, pour cette magnifique visite. Je vous en remercie, cher monsieur Diallo, parce que je crois qu'ici nous illustrons très concrètement la réalité du partenariat entre la France et la Guinée. Un partenariat de confiance, un partenariat durable, de long terme, un partenariat gagnant-gagnant, et un partenariat crédible, et au service des populations », a-t-il déclaré. Pour le diplomate français, l’extension de SOGUIPAL répond à l’ambition de développer la transformation locale et de renforcer les capacités industrielles du pays. « Ça illustre parfaitement cette ambition, grâce à Proparco, évidemment, filiale du groupe Agence Française de Développement, dédiée au secteur privé, qui vient d'accorder ce prêt de 5 millions d'euros à SOGUIPAL. C'est un programme d'investissement, il faut le dire, parce qu'aujourd'hui, la Guinée investit dans son avenir », a-t-il poursuivi. Luc Briard a également évoqué la stratégie Simandou 2040, estimant que cette vision de développement à long terme contribue à rassurer les investisseurs étrangers. Au cours de son intervention, il a insisté sur les efforts de l’entreprise en matière de formation du personnel, de maîtrise de la qualité et de gestion de la chaîne du froid, un défi important pour la conservation et la distribution des produits alimentaires en Guinée. L'approvisionnement local au cœur des perspectives Au-delà des équipements et de l’augmentation de la production, l’approvisionnement en matières premières locales constitue un autre enjeu évoqué au cours de la visite. Luc Briard a fait état d’une perspective d’organisation de l’approvisionnement en lait frais à partir de Forécariah, une initiative qui pourrait contribuer à rapprocher les producteurs locaux des unités de transformation. « Et évidemment, c'est une très bonne nouvelle, parce que Conakry est un immense marché, a besoin de produits qui viennent de l'intérieur du pays. Ce sera un facteur de désenclavement pour des milliers de producteurs guinéens. Et donc l'enjeu dépasse évidemment votre seule entreprise », a-t-il indiqué. Le diplomate a également souligné le potentiel de développement de la filière laitière guinéenne, alors que la production nationale ne couvre encore qu’une faible partie des besoins du marché. « En Guinée, la production locale ne couvre aujourd'hui qu'une faible partie des besoins en produits laitiers. Le reste est trop souvent importé. Il y a là donc une marge de manœuvre pour la souveraineté alimentaire, et vous êtes un de ces soldats de cette guerre économique, et bravo pour cela. Parce que vous évitez aux familles guinéennes la variation des prix internationaux, le coût du transport, les ruptures d'approvisionnement », a-t-il déclaré. Pour lui, le développement des capacités de transformation sur place doit permettre de renforcer la souveraineté alimentaire, de stabiliser l’offre et de créer davantage de valeur ajoutée en Guinée. Les autorités guinéennes saluent un investissement stratégique Les représentants des ministères de l’Industrie et du Commerce et du Plan et de la Coopération internationale ont, de leur côté, salué le développement de SOGUIPAL, présenté comme un exemple de l’importance de l’investissement privé dans la transformation économique du pays. Le chef de cabinet du ministère de l’Industrie et du Commerce a notamment mis en avant le parcours entrepreneurial d’Ibrahima Diallo et la place de son entreprise dans le secteur agroalimentaire. « En fait, on part du commerce général à une aventure entrepreneuriale dans le secteur de l'industrie. Le parcours de Elhadj Ibrahima est enviable. C'est un parcours à saluer, et je tiens avant tout propos à le saluer. Elhadj, bravo », a-t-il déclaré. Il a ensuite rappelé le caractère stratégique de cette activité pour l’industrie nationale. « Dans le secteur du lait, dans le secteur du yaourt, c'est un fleuron pour l'industrie nationale. C'est une industrie stratégique pour nous, dans le sous-secteur de l'agro-business. C'est une des priorités, comme vous le savez, du programme de développement socio-économique durable et responsable, Simandou 2040, porté par son excellence, Mamadi Doumbouya, Président de la République de Guinée », a-t-il souligné. Le secrétaire général du ministère du Plan et de la Coopération internationale a, pour sa part, salué la contribution de ce type d’investissement à la transformation structurelle de l’économie guinéenne, tout en réaffirmant la volonté des autorités de soutenir les initiatives qui favorisent la production locale. Il a également évoqué la possibilité de développer des mini-laiteries pour mieux absorber la production de lait issue de l’intérieur du pays et limiter les pertes. « Toujours pour parler de Coyah, on a évoqué le sujet des mini-laiteries en Guinée, qui permettraient justement de mieux absorber la production de l'intérieur et éviter le gaspillage », a-t-il expliqué. Les deux responsables ont ainsi mis en avant la nécessité de renforcer les activités de transformation, de valoriser les ressources locales et de faire du développement industriel un levier de création d’emplois. Un investissement au-delà de la production de yaourt Avec un programme d’investissement de 7,2 millions d’euros, dont 5 millions financés par Proparco, SOGUIPAL entend consolider son outil industriel et accroître sa présence sur le marché guinéen. Le passage annoncé de 9 à 15 tonnes de yaourt par jour représente une augmentation de capacité d’environ 67 %, tandis que les 30 emplois directs prévus constituent une retombée attendue du projet. Au-delà de la croissance de l’entreprise, l’enjeu concerne également la structuration de la filière laitière, le développement de circuits d’approvisionnement locaux et la réduction de la dépendance aux importations. La signature du partenariat était annoncée dans la soirée à l’ambassade de France en Guinée. Ce financement marque une nouvelle étape dans la collaboration entre PROPARCO et SOGUIPAL, avec l’ambition de soutenir l’investissement privé et de renforcer la production agroalimentaire en Guinée. Christine Finda Kamano L’article SOGUIPAL bénéficie d’un financement de 5 millions d’euros de Proparco pour porter la production de Best Yaourt à 15 tonnes par jour est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Ghanaian veterinarian leads campaign against proposed African battery cage standard
items.description: A prominent Ghanaian veterinarian is leading a continent-wide campaign against a proposed standard from the African Organisation for Standardisation (ARSO) that would approve battery cages for egg-laying hens. Dr. Daniel Baba Abiliba, founder of the Animal Welfare League (AWL) and a graduate student at the Yale School of the Environment, is speaking out against ARSO’s draft standard, CD-ARS 1241:2025(E), which would formally accept the worst form of battery cages as a housing system for laying hens. “The battery cage system ARSO is endorsing is horrible, and it runs contrary to African ideals,” Dr. Abiliba said. “Most Africans interact with animals in one way or another, in our homes, on our farms and in our communities. Also, a large number of us know that chickens are sentient beings; they can feel pain, fear, and distress. The battery cage system has been found to contribute a lot of pain and suffering to chickens. This standard does not reflect who we are.” The Pan-African Campaign Together with coalition partners, AWL launched a campaign in March 2026 at stoparsobatterycages.org . It calls on all 44 African national standards bodies to reject the draft by signing the petition. “Treating animals well is not at odds with productivity,” Dr. Abiliba said. “Ghanaian farmers know that healthy, well-kept animals are productive animals. We don’t have to choose between caring for animals and feeding our people.” Ghana’s Leadership in Animal Welfare Ghana has demonstrated strong leadership in establishing national poultry welfare standards through the creation of GS 1404:2026 (Farm Animal Welfare – Requirements for Poultry). Dr. Abiliba contributed directly to this effort as part of the technical committee that drafted the standard alongside the Ghana Standards Authority (GSA), the Veterinary Services Directorate (VSD), and other key stakeholders. The GSA has officially adopted both the standard and its accompanying inspection manual as national benchmarks. In line with this, the VSD is currently piloting implementation across over 100 farms nationwide. “Good animal husbandry has always been part of the African farming tradition. This standard simply puts it into writing and GS 1404 builds on what our farmers already know. ARSO should be learning from Ghana, not moving in the opposite direction,” Dr Abiliba said. A veterinarian with a global record Dr. Abiliba is currently pursuing a Master of Environmental Management at the Yale School of the Environment in the United States. He earned his Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). He was the first Ghanaian to win the MSD/World Veterinary Association Veterinary Student Scholarship and his exemplary work in rabies prevention has been recognised by the World Health Organization. The future of animal welfare in Africa depends on collective action. Readers, farmers, and organizations are urged to join the campaign against battery cages by visiting stoparsobatterycages.org and calling on African national standards bodies to reject draft standard CD-ARS 1241:2025(E).

items.title: JI to 'no longer' postpone Islamabad march against petrol levy, says will resume it in mid-November
items.description: Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman on Tuesday said his party would hold its march to Islamabad against the petroleum levy in mid-November. He made the announcement during a press conference in Islamabad, which came shortly after he met with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to discuss his demand to abolish the petroleum levy. “We want to make it clear that we will not postpone our Islamabad march any longer. It will now take place in mid-November, and it certainly will take place,” the JI chief said. He added, “Let them announce this package, provide this relief, and devise a mechanism to abolish this extortionate levy before that, [but] if they do not do so, we might have to sit on the road to talk. “We are prepared for anything,” Rehman declared. Asked about the outcome of his meeting with PM Shehbaz — offered by the latter when urging the party to postpone its Islamabad march — the JI emir refrained from terming it “inconclusive”. He noted that two sides had consensus on expanding the scope of relief, but there were disagreements over the “modalities” and “procedure”. “We say eliminate the levy; they say we can move towards it phase by phase,” Rehman elaborated. At around 4pm, a post on JI’s account said Rehman had reached PM House, accompanied by a delegation including the party’s Deputy Emir Liaquat Baloch, Deputy Secretary General Syed Farasat Shah, and JI Islamabad Emir Nasrullah Randhawa. Rehman told the media that JI was forming another committee on the matter, comprising Baloch, Shah and Randhawa. “We cannot simply accept peanuts,” the JI chief said when asked about a reported government offer to reduce the levies by Rs20-30. He stressed that his party stood firm on its stance. He maintained that JI would continue its preparations and would begin nationwide mobilisation for its planned march to the federal capital, while negotiations would also continue at the same time. “Our preparations are already complete; we will prepare further [and] we will talk to them (the government) further. However, we will also hold the Islamabad march in mid-November,” Rehman said. Asked whether JI had presented any alternative to abolishing the levy, he responded in the affirmative, asserting that his party had comprehensive preparations. Rehman highlighted that all past governments vowed not to take loans from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) but then entered into programmes with it after coming into power. He said his party pointed this out, adding, “Give relief to the people; do not take retribution for your incompetence from the nation.” The JI has been demanding for over two months that the Centre abolish petroleum levies, as fuel prices have skyrocketed due to conflicts in the Middle East since March. The Centre and JI had agreed to form committees in early September — when the latter had planned a nationwide strike — to recommend measures to reduce the levy. Rehman on Monday warned that the party would march to Islamabad in mid-November if the premier did not abolish the petroleum levy. On Aug 16, the JI announced sit-ins in all the provincial capitals of Pakistan against the petroleum levy and had called for a nationwide strike on Sept 3. On Sept 20, the party launched a protest march towards Islamabad, warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the protest could turn into one to oust the government. On Sept 22, the JI emir said his party, whose convoy had reached Multan, was postponing its long march at the request of PM Shehbaz, who had assured the other side of a meeting to discuss the matters. However, in a press release issued last week, the party alleged that the government had made no further contact regarding the planned meeting.

items.title: We Can All Make Life Feel Like a Movie. Should We?
items.description: Any traveler knows that a hotel gym can be the saddest place on earth. The low ceiling; the mere inches between weights and treadmills; the tiny, disintegration-ready water cups—everything conveys that you’re there to briefly repent for a salty travel diet and then get out as quickly as you can. But every modern traveler also knows that headphones can make the chore feel transcendent. A beat pumps, endorphins build, and maybe you throw in a round on the rowing machine just because. Suddenly, you’re inside a Lil Wayne or Bruce Springsteen song—feeling like a baller, a hero. The jail cell by the second-floor ice machine becomes a movie set, and you’re the star. This is the experience that the then-unknown singer Sophia Stel captured last year, in her music video for “I’ll Take It,” a synth-pop track that caught buzz on TikTok and has drawn nearly 14 million Spotify plays. In the video, the 20-something Canadian wears a purple hoodie and wired earbuds to work out in a dimly lit Sheraton gym. No music-video freakiness happens—it’s not like the stationary bike turns into a Harley. But Stel just seems so blissed-out as she sweats to lyrics about being interesting and hot (“I’m tortured, you love it, you hate it / You think about me naked”). At the end, she bounds out into a beige hallway—her inner self changed, her outer world not. The video helps explain how Stel earned the distinction of being one of the first artists signed to A24 Music. Yes, A24, as in the movie studio behind dozens of acclaimed indies , including Moonlight , Everything Everywhere All at Once , and this year’s mindbending hits Backrooms and You Can See Everything . Since launching in 2012, A24 has become so revered that its branded baseball hats are now hipster totems . In 2025, the record label that it had previously used to distribute soundtracks started to sign singers with no apparent connections to its films. The studio’s press-shy leaders have maintained mystery about their intentions, but Stel’s music, at least, fits the larger trend that A24 has helped drive: a cultural rethinking of the meaning of cinematic . The studio funds lots of different kinds of work—action flicks, intimate comedies, topical documentaries—so it’s hard to pin down any singular A24 aesthetic. Still, film buffs like to debate the “know it when you see it” quality that unites its output. Is it the muted colors? Is it the tepid pacing? Fundamentally, those attributes serve a deeper trick: scrambling the viewers’ sense of what’s ordinary and what’s filmic. Office back rooms turn horrific; an audit bureau gets a sci-fi twist ; Elizabeth Holmes’s rental house becomes suffused with Hitchcockian paranoia . A24’s films make banal settings feel uncanny through small stylistic choices—sometimes, only a music cue. Perhaps not coincidentally, the studio has risen in an era when technology encourages people to experience their lives in movielike ways. Decades ago, the Walkman and then the iPod gave consumers the ability to replace the noise of commutes and chores with more satisfying soundtracks. Streaming and smartphones then supercharged that practice—and gave movie scores a second life as sources of on-the-go vibes (to use a term synonymous with A24). Phone cameras and video-sharing platforms have further pushed people to see life through the lens of entertainment . The idea that we’re all performers was once a theory of postmodern scholars; now it’s taken for granted in rap lyrics (Lil Nas X: “My life is a movie”) and TikTok slang (“main-character energy”). The result is that cinematic , as a descriptor, now connotes not a break from regular life but an enhancement of it. Once, the term would have conjured the symphonic grandeur of a John Williams score—or at least the alien soundscapes of Tangerine Dream. Film-obsessed popular musicians made concept albums that insisted on their own importance, such as the Who’s Tommy . But a lot of today’s movie-influenced music is happy to simmer in the background. The Tim Burton–inspired whispers of Billie Eilish, the spaghetti-Western bustle of Khruangbin, or the folktronica of the A24-signed Ear cast an intriguing mood without necessarily demanding intense attention. (Which is not to say those musicians don’t reward close listening.) [ Read: The new sound of sexual frustration ] Stel makes blurry, nocturnal pop that comports with this approach: “In general, my music tends to be soundtrack-like,” she told Office magazine. “To me it’s meant to be listened to on your walk home with headphones in.” But at the same time, it’s about that sort of listening. She was raised as one of 11 kids in a strictly religious family; the radio was mostly banned. In late adolescence, she discovered Drake, Future, and Rihanna: artists whose songs about holding court in crowded nightclubs was, to a historically unprecedented extent, enjoyed through earbuds. The title of her debut album, the greatest album of all time —released by A24 earlier this month—is like a joke about being an ordinary mortal who uses music to feel extraordinary. Working on her laptop to arrange sparse but anthemic songs, Stel gravitates toward crunchy synth textures that feel cheap and handmade. She sings in an Auto-Tuned mumble that seems to indicate an indifference to being understood, but her melodies and riffs frequently evoke the blustering trap, EDM, and pop of the 2010s. Her lyrics swerve back and forth between burned-out sadness and confident head rushes enabled by drugs or sex (“Saying stupid things like ‘I’m the chosen one’”). Her songs are about chasing a climax and not caring if it’s artificial, and the fun of listening to her lies in the way that glum monotony inevitably gives way to a zooming high. She’s not the only musician making meta-cinematic work lately. As I wrote a couple of months ago, Slayyyter and Tinashe are drawing hype with disappointment-tinged pop about the ever-widening gap between Hollywood’s vision of the American dream and the distracted, disconnected culture in which it exists. The ascendent Irish rock band Fontaines D.C. just released a seductive, nightmarish album, Dopamine Chamber , that’s inspired by the feeling of living inside a screen. To get in the proper headspace to write, the front man, Grian Chatten, went to a theater and sat through most of a movie while listening to music in his headphones. “The sense of isolation from that was unreal,” he told The New York Times . That experience may sound extreme—but there’s a reason the subject of derealization is culturally pervasive right now, whether the example is Stel’s Lynchian party anthems or the trippy layers of You Can See Everything . As we flick between amusements on our phones and experiences in the real world, figuring out which sensations and memories are authentically our own becomes difficult. Art and media can help lend us a sense of meaning and narrative, but to really script our own story, we need to take off the headphones from time to time.

items.title: Charles Bissue: The man who wants a trial but challenges the trial
items.description: Charles Bissue is an interesting accused person. He says he wants a speedy trial and accuses the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) of delaying his day in court. Yet, his own legal history raises questions about how eager he has been to let the investigation and prosecution proceed. The OSP’s published records tell part of the story. Since 2023, he has filed 7 cases in respect of a case filed in 2025. The suits include the following: Suit No. J5/8/2025: Republic vs. High Court, Accra Human Rights Division (Court 2); Ex Parte Charles Bissue – Applicant, Office of the Special Prosecutor and Attorney-General – Interested Parties. Suit No. GJ/0098/2023: Republic vs. Office of the Special Prosecutor; Ex Parte Charles Bissue. Suit No. J8/08/2025: Republic vs. High Court, Accra Human Rights Division (Court 2); Ex Parte Charles Bissue – Applicant, Office of the Special Prosecutor and Attorney-General – Interested Parties. Suit No. GJ/0928/2023: Republic vs. District Court, Kaneshie and Office of the Special Prosecutor; Ex Parte Charles Bissue. Suit No. HR/0094/2023: Charles Bissue vs. Office of the Special Prosecutor Suit No. GJ/0358/2023: Charles Bissue vs. OSP, Anas Aremeyaw Anas and Tiger Eye P.I. Suit No. HR/0101/2023: Charles Bissue vs. Kaneshie District Court. h. Suit No. H3/458/2025: Charles Bissue vs. Office of the Special Prosecution, Kaneshie District Court. These are not minor details. They show that legal proceedings initiated by Bissue formed part of the history that preceded his prosecution. Yet, through sections of the media, he has suggested that he has been standing trial since 2017. The OSP was established in 2018. Investigations, civil litigation and criminal trials are not the same thing. One cannot simply collapse them into a single timeline. The OSP eventually filed fresh criminal proceedings on 1 July 2025 under CR/0559/2025, The Republic v Charles Cromwell Nanabanyin Onuawonto Bissue & 2 Ors . Bissue faces nine counts relating to corruption and abuse of public office. Raphael Mensah and Dr Naa Dedei Tagoe are charged in connection with the alleged scheme. All three pleaded not guilty. The case is not about whether Bissue considers the alleged amount small. It concerns allegations that public office was compromised to facilitate the issuance of a concession sticker enabling a business entity to commence mining without a licence. If proved, the alleged conduct would raise serious questions about the integrity of the public process, regardless of the amount involved. Thomas Andy Owusu, who was charged in the earlier case, pleaded guilty and was convicted in June 2025 under a plea agreement. His conviction does not establish Bissue’s guilt, which remains for the court to determine. Now, the dispute has shifted to whether the earlier case was properly discontinued and whether the current proceedings can continue. His lawyers have also raised arguments concerning an earlier police investigation and alleged conflict of interest involving the Special Prosecutor’s past professional association with Anas Aremeyaw Anas. These arguments must be assessed against the relevant court records and rulings. But the central contradiction remains: how does one repeatedly demand a speedy trial while pursuing legal challenges that may prevent the trial from proceeding? Bissue has every right to challenge the prosecution. The court must determine those objections fairly. But a procedural dispute is not automatically the end of a criminal case, just as a prosecution is not proof of guilt. The OSP should not be interested in winning a public-relations contest. Its duty is to pursue justice. If the evidence fails, Bissue must be acquitted. If the prosecution proves its case, the law must take its course. A speedy trial should lead to a judicial determination—not become a slogan used against the prosecution while the proceedings themselves are being challenged.

items.title: Troops kill 8 terrorists, recover weapons in Kaduna, Zamfara
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma (OPFY) have neutralised 8 suspected armed terrorists and rescued 3 kidnapped victims in coordinated operations conducted in Katsina, Kaduna and Zamfara States. According to a statement by Captain Tamuno Sinive, Media Information Officer, the operations also led to the recovery of an AK-47 rifle, 3 locally fabricated guns, 3 motorcycles, cutlasses and assorted charms from the terrorists. He said, “On Saturday 24 October 2026, troops of Sector one received a distress call from farmers at Machika Dam, Sabuwa Local Government Area of Katsina State, reporting terrorist activities in the area. “The troops promptly mobilised to the location and engaged the terrorists in a gun battle, resulting in the neutralization of two terrorists, while others fled the area. “In the course of the operation, troops also rescued Mr Suleiman Umar, aged 42, who had been kidnapped by the terrorists. ‘Further exploitation of the area led to the recovery of one AK-47 rifle with a magazine containing rounds of ammunition, as well as one motorcycle. “In another incident on the same day, troops of Sector one, in conjunction with the Civilian Joint Task Force (CJTF), foiled a terrorist ambush along Ungwan Iya, Igabi Local Government Area of Kaduna State, neutralising 6 suspected terrorists. “During the operation, the troops recovered three locally fabricated guns, 2 motorcycles, cutlasses and assorted charms. “The incident occurred when the troops responded to a distress call reporting an attack by suspected armed terrorists at Ungwan Mallami village, during which the terrorists fled with two kidnapped victims. “However, while trailing the terrorists, the troops came under attack but responded swiftly with superior firepower, resulting in the neutralization of the terrorists, while others fled in disarray. “Similarly, troops of Sector 2, rescued two kidnapped victims in Bagega, Anka Local Government Area of Zamfara State, on Sunday, 25 October 2026. “The rescued victims were identified conducting as Mr Shehu Chete, aged 40, and Mr Bugu Bedi, aged 25, both indigenes of Kebbi State. “The troops, while conducting surveillance operations in the general area, observed the activities of suspected terrorists and swiftly responded with a fighting patrol. “On sighting the troops, the terrorists fled the area, abandoning the 2 victims. “The rescued victims were immediately evacuated to Bagega Clinic for medical attention before being moved to the military base for further assessment and subsequent reunion with their families. “Troops are currently dominating the general areas through sustained patrols and search operations aimed at apprehending the terrorists, rescuing kidnapped victims and preventing further attacks towards ensuring the safety of residents. “The Theatre Commander, Joint Task Force North West, Operation has commended the troops of Fansan Yamma for their gallantry and resilience in responding to the attacks. “Members of the public are urged to continue supporting ongoing military operations by providing timely and credible information on suspicious movements and activities within their communities.” The post Troops kill 8 terrorists, recover weapons in Kaduna, Zamfara appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Minority demands independent probe into S.A evacuation case
items.description: The Minority in Parliament has called for an independent investigation into Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs over the controversy surrounding the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa. The caucus says an independent probe is necessary to establish the facts surrounding the GH¢49.72 million reportedly spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians between May 27 and September 4, 2026, amid renewed xenophobic attacks. The Minority, during a press conference on Tuesday, October 27, raised concerns about alleged gaps in flight records, inconsistencies in payment registers and duplicate entries in documents relating to the evacuation. “Given the gravity of these revelations and in order to ensure an impartial investigation into the matter, we call on the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Honourable Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, to resign immediately. His handling of this exercise has brought his high office into disrepute,” Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, said. It has also questioned payments for reintegration and transport allowances, arguing that the issues require thorough scrutiny to establish whether there were any financial or administrative irregularities. READ ALSO: Minority demands Ablakwa’s resignation or dismissal over SA evacuation payments The controversy follows the release of documents by the Ministry in response to a Right to Information request, which the Minority says contain discrepancies that require further investigation. Mr Ablakwa has denied allegations of financial impropriety, insisting that the evacuation expenditure is accounted for. He has also called for an independent audit of evacuation exercises undertaken since 2017, including the South Africa operation. The Minority says the investigation must establish accountability and ensure transparency in the management of public funds. It has consequently demanded the immediate resignation of Mr Ablakwa, warning that it will call on President John Dramani Mahama to dismiss him if he fails to step down. The caucus has threatened to initiate a vote of censure against the Minister in Parliament if its demand is not met.

items.title: Edo Voter Register: Utomi, others demand INEC explanation over alleged AI-generated images
items.description: By Emmanuel Okogba Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) chieftain and economist, Prof. Pat Utomi, has raised concerns over allegations that artificial intelligence (AI)-generated photographs appear in the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) online voter register in parts of Edo State. Utomi’s reaction followed posts by social media user Decosule, who called on INEC to explain the presence of what he described as AI-generated images in voter records displayed on the commission’s website. Decosule shared screenshots purportedly taken from the online voter register for polling units in Ward 11, Etsako West Local Government Area, and Udomi in Esan Central Local Government Area, questioning the authenticity of some photographs. He asked the electoral commission to clarify how the images were included in the register, who conducted the voter registration or image-capturing process, and whether the Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) associated with the entries had been collected. In a post reacting to the issue, Utomi warned that questions surrounding the images could undermine public confidence in the country’s electoral process if not properly addressed. “INEC cannot afford to be careless with the credibility of Nigeria’s electoral process. The presence of AI-generated images in a register meant to support our democracy raises serious questions about verification, transparency and accountability. Our democracy is at stake here!” Utomi wrote. Decosule had also claimed to have observed similar images in the register for Udomi in Esan Central, the local government area associated with Edo State Governor Monday Okpebholo. The screenshots shared by Decosule showed voter entries under polling units identified as Iyoku–Utukwe Afashio Booth and Ikabigbo I–Ikabigbo Primary School in Etsako West, as well as Udomi Primary School in Esan Central. Decosule urged INEC to provide an explanation, particularly regarding the origin of the photographs and the processes used to verify voter information. However, the screenshots alone do not independently establish that the images were generated using AI or demonstrate whether any irregularities occurred during voter registration. INEC is yet to provide an official response to clarify the authenticity of the photographs, how they came to appear on the online platform and whether the commission had identified any problems with the records. items.title: Ghana must move from ESG policy commitments to action – Local Government Minister
items.description: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has called for stronger institutional coordination, sustainable financing and accountability mechanisms to accelerate the adoption of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) principles across Ghana’s economy. He said integrating ESG considerations into national policies, institutional practices and private sector operations was essential to promoting responsible investment, protecting natural resources and creating sustainable economic opportunities. Addressing the Ghana National Climate and ESG Policy Summit 2026 at the Mövenpick Ambassador Hotel in Accra on Tuesday, October 27, the Minister said Ghana must move beyond policy commitments to practical and measurable action. “The integration of Environmental, Social and Governance principles into national policies, institutional practices and private-sector operations is therefore not merely a matter of compliance or corporate responsibility. It is a strategic imperative,” he said. He explained that effective implementation would require stronger coordination among government institutions, increased mobilisation of sustainable finance and meaningful partnerships with the private sector, development partners, academia and civil society. The Minister also emphasised the importance of transparency, accountability, institutional capacity and reliable data in advancing sustainability practices. “Public and private institutions alike must be encouraged to adopt credible sustainability practices, strengthen environmental and social risk management, and report their progress against clearly defined standards and measurable indicators,” he said. He noted that the scale and complexity of climate change required a coordinated national response supported by sustained commitment, adequate financing and effective implementation. “Government, on its part, remains committed to advancing policies and partnerships that support climate resilience, environmental protection, sustainable investment and responsible governance,” he added. The Minister urged participants to ensure that the summit produced concrete policy recommendations and institutional commitments rather than ending with discussions alone. “This Summit must therefore serve as more than a forum for discussion. It must be a catalyst for concrete policy recommendations, institutional commitments and actionable strategies,” he said. He welcomed plans for the summit to conclude with a National Communiqué, noting that his ministry would work with local assemblies to advance recommendations relevant to local government. The summit brought together government officials, local government leaders, private sector representatives, development partners and civil society organisations to discuss strategies for strengthening climate resilience and promoting ESG principles in Ghana.

items.title: GPL 2026/27: ‘I will resign if Samartex engages in match-fixing’ – GM Edmund Ackah
items.description: FC Samartex 1996 General Manager Edmund Ackah has vowed to resign from his position if the club is found to be involved in match-fixing or any illegal activity. Ackah made the declaration amid concerns over reports linking the club to match manipulation and the absence of several of their matches from television coverage. Speaking in an interview with Asempa FM, the experienced football administrator said he had confidence in the club’s leadership and management. “I will resign from FC Samartex if the club engages in anything illegal or match-fixing,” he stated. “I have heard that our games are not on television because of where we are located and the distance, but that is not fair,” he added. “Our stadium is safe because there are CCTV cameras everywhere, so I don’t know why there will be that decision not to air our games.” The 2024 Ghana Premier League champions currently sit third on the league table. Matchday nine will see Samartex hosts Bibiani Gold Stars at the Nsenkyire Sports Arena on Sunday November 1.

items.title: Assemblies must lead Ghana’s climate response – Local Government Minister
items.description: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has called on Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) to take a leading role in Ghana’s response to climate change, urging them to translate national commitments into practical results at the community level. He said the effects of climate change, including flooding, drought, pressure on land and water resources, and threats to farming livelihoods, were being felt directly in districts, making local government institutions central to the country’s green transition. Speaking at the Ghana National Climate and ESG Policy Summit 2026 at the Mövenpick Ambassador Hotel in Accra on Tuesday, October 27, the Minister said climate considerations must be incorporated into the development plans and budgets of local assemblies. “Much of that action will happen at the local level. It is in our districts that the effects of climate change are felt first,” he said. He added that national commitments could only produce meaningful results if local authorities were equipped with the capacity and resources to implement climate policies effectively. “Decentralising the green transition means mainstreaming climate and ESG considerations into the medium-term development plans and budgets of our Assemblies; strengthening the capacity of our Assemblies to plan, finance, deliver and report on climate action,” he said. The Minister said his ministry would continue to collaborate with the Office of the Minister of State for Climate Change and Sustainability, the Ministry of Environment, Science and Technology, the District Assemblies Common Fund (DACF), the National Association of Local Authorities of Ghana and development partners to advance the agenda. He also highlighted the role of traditional authorities in climate action, describing them as “essential partners” because of their position as custodians of land and natural resources. The Minister further stressed the need to ensure that climate policies addressed the needs of vulnerable communities, women, young people and people whose livelihoods depended directly on the natural environment. “A just and equitable transition must remain central to our development agenda, ensuring that the benefits of climate action are broadly shared and that no community is left behind,” he said. He urged local government leaders to demonstrate commitment to climate action by ensuring that the decisions and recommendations emerging from the summit are translated into tangible improvements in their respective communities.

items.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval to expand transfer of convicted offenders agreements
items.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina President Bola Tinubu has transmitted a bill seeking to amend the Transfer of Convicted Offenders (Enactment and Enforcement) Act to the House of Representatives for consideration, with a view to extending its application to countries outside the Commonwealth. In a letter dated October 20, 2026, addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, Tinubu urged lawmakers to consider the proposed legislation expeditiously. The bill, titled Transfer of Convicted Offenders (Enactment and Enforcement) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeks to amend the existing law, Cap. T16, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. According to the President, the proposed amendment is designed to give effect to schemes or agreements between the Federal Government of Nigeria and other countries for the transfer of convicted offenders. The amendment would also empower the President, through an order published in the Federal Gazette, to extend the application of the Act to any country with which Nigeria has entered into such an agreement. Tinubu said the proposed change would enable Nigeria to implement agreements concluded with countries outside the Commonwealth, potentially broadening the scope of international cooperation on the transfer of convicted offenders. Transmitting the bill pursuant to Section 58(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the President formally requested the consideration of the House of Representatives. “While it is my hope that the House of Representatives will consider this submission expeditiously, please accept, Rt. Hon. Speaker, the assurances of my highest consideration,” Tinubu stated in the letter. The bill is now before the House for consideration. The presidential communication did not specify the countries that could be covered by future agreements or provide details of the proposed implementation arrangements. items.title: Infrastructures | Rencontre à Tunis autour du salon Intermat Paris 2027
items.description: La Chambre de commerce et d’industrie tuniso-française (CCITF)organise une rencontre d’échanges autour du salon «Intermat Paris 2027 : Construire les infrastructures de demain – Enjeux et perspectives de la Tunisie à l’Afrique», le mardi 3 novembre 2026, de 8h30 à 12h, au Novotel Tunis – Berges du Lac 2. La rencontre, qui sera présidée par Khelil Chaibi, président de la CCITF, verra pa participation de Guillaume Schaeffer, directeur du salon Intermat, et de Laura Sanchez, directrice de la communication de la manifestation. Les échanges porteront sur les principaux enjeux du secteur en Tunisie, notamment la modernisation des infrastructures, le développement du réseau routier, les grands projets et l’évolution des besoins en équipements et en technologies. Des représentants du ministère de l’Equipement et de l’Habitatet dela Fédération nationale des entrepreneurs de bâtiment et de travaux publics, relevant de l’Union tunisienne de l’industrie, du commerce et de l’artisanat (Utica) sont attendus pour partager leurs perspectives sur les priorités du secteur. Organisé du 21 au 24 avril 2027 à Paris-Nord Villepinte, Intermat est un salon de référence dédié aux équipements, aux technologies et aux solutions pour la construction et les travaux publics. Il rassemble les professionnels des grands chantiers, du terrassement et des infrastructures, ainsi que les fabricants, distributeurs et donneurs d’ordre, autour des innovations et des opportunités de partenariat dans le secteur. L’édition 2027 accordera également une place aux enjeux de coopération et de développement des marchés africains, à travers l’African Summit. Cette rencontre à Tunis permettra aux professionnels de mieux appréhender les opportunités offertes par Intermat Paris 2027 et de renforcer les échanges entre les acteurs tunisiens, français et africains. items.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval for ₦269.4bn promissory notes to settle FG debts
items.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to approve the establishment and expansion of the Federal Government’s Promissory Note Programme to settle outstanding verified liabilities totalling ₦269.44bn. This was contained in a letter by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume which was read on the floor of the House during plenary in Abuja. The request is aimed at addressing outstanding contractual, project-related and other financial obligations owed to various categories of creditors. In a letter dated August 18, 2026, and received by the Office of the Speaker on October 21, Akume said the liabilities amounted to ₦269,446,402,822.56, following a comprehensive review by relevant ministries, departments and agencies. He said Tinubu had approved the proposal to establish and expand the programme as a mechanism for settling the verified obligations. According to the letter, the programme is designed to provide “a structured, transparent and fiscally responsible framework” for settling the outstanding debts, while ensuring that only verified and validated claims are admitted. The President is seeking legislative approval for the issuance of promissory notes worth ₦269.44bn, or such other amount as may be approved by the National Assembly, to settle the liabilities contained in the accompanying schedule. The request also seeks approval for the inclusion of the identified categories of liabilities and beneficiaries in the programme, subject to final verification, reconciliation and certification by the relevant government agencies. Tinubu further asked the National Assembly to authorise the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, in collaboration with the Debt Management Office and other relevant agencies, to take the necessary steps to implement the programme. Akume explained that the proposal was intended to mitigate the continued accumulation of interest, penalties and other financial costs associated with the outstanding obligations. He said the arrangement would also provide relief to affected creditors and strengthen confidence in the Federal Government’s commitment to honouring legitimate contractual and other obligations. The SGF noted that the Federal Government had previously used the Promissory Note Programme to settle inherited local debts and contractual obligations, following Federal Executive Council approval and subsequent National Assembly approval. He added that the proposed arrangement was expected to facilitate the orderly settlement of the liabilities without imposing an immediate and disproportionate cash-flow burden on the Federal Government. According to the letter, the programme would also support fiscal planning by spreading repayment obligations over an appropriate period in line with prudent debt management principles. Akume urged the House to give the request urgent consideration, citing the magnitude and age of some of the outstanding liabilities and the possibility of further accumulation of interest and associated costs. He said early legislative approval would enable the Federal Government to commence the necessary processes for issuing the promissory notes and bringing the affected liabilities to a close. The detailed schedule of the liabilities, including the relevant categories, beneficiaries, amounts and supporting documentation, was forwarded to the National Assembly for consideration. items.title: Tinubu writes Senate, seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects
items.description: …As Senate refers 2026–2027 supplementary borrowing plan to debt committee, gives one week to report By Henry Umoru President Bola Tinubu has written the Senate, seeking approval of a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion to finance infrastructure and development projects across the country. President Tinubu’s letter was addressed to the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio. Akpabio, who read the letter on Tuesday during plenary, said the request covers the 2026–2027 fiscal period and targets critical sectors, including power, transportation, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply and security. Tinubu, who noted that the proposed borrowing was necessary to bridge Nigeria’s infrastructure funding gap, sustain economic growth, generate employment and improve the living conditions of Nigerians, urged the National Assembly to give the plan urgent consideration and approval to facilitate the timely release of funds and implementation of the projects. In the letter, the president said the proposed external financing would support projects and programmes spanning virtually every sector of the economy. “The 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan cuts across all sectors, with specific emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, health, education, water supply, growth, security and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms, amongst others,” he said. According to the letter, the proposed facilities total $20,517,755,901 and €1,045,083,643, and the projects had been selected after technical and economic assessments. “I want to emphasise that the projects and programmes included in the Borrowing Plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country,” he said. The president who explained that the proposed investments were expected to create employment opportunities, promote skills acquisition, encourage entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and strengthen food security, said, “These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skills acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improve the livelihood of the Nigerian child.” He disclosed that most of the projects would be executed across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, stressing that the nationwide spread of the interventions would help address development needs across the federation, adding that the scale of Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit and the financial resources required to address it have made additional external borrowing necessary. “In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue broader external borrowings to close the financing shortfall,” Tinubu said. He identified power, transportation and healthcare as among the critical sectors expected to benefit from the proposed financing. “These funds will primarily be directed towards critical infrastructure projects in various sectors, including power, transportation and healthcare, amongst others,” the president said. Tinubu, who maintained that prompt consideration of the request would enable the government to meet its obligations to Nigerians through timely disbursement of funds and effective execution of the projects, said, “Given the urgent nature of these needs and the importance of stabilising the country, it is crucial to seek the consideration and approval of the National Assembly leadership and the entire National Assembly for the 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan.” The President, who noted that legislative approval would enable the government to proceed with the proposed interventions, said, “This will enable the government to fulfil its obligations to the Nigerian people through timely disbursements and effective project implementation.” The President of the Senate thereafter referred the Communication to the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts for further legislative action to report at plenary within one week. The Committee is expected to examine the proposal, potentially in collaboration with the Senate Committee on Appropriations and other relevant committees. The letter, as presented to the Senate, did not provide a detailed project-by-project breakdown of the proposed facilities, the specific financing terms or the amount earmarked for each sector. The National Assembly’s consideration of the request is expected to focus on the proposed financing and its intended development objectives, including the government’s plan to close infrastructure gaps, stimulate economic activities and improve public services. The letter titled “Federal Government 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plans, read, ” I write in reference to the above subjects and to submit the attached Federal Government 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plans for consideration and early approval of the National Assembly to ensure prompt implementation of our projects. “The 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan cuts across all sectors with specific emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, health, education, water supply, growth, security, and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms, amongst others. “The total facility for the projects and programs under the Borrowing Growing Plan is $20,517,000,000 and €1,045,083,643 respectively and the summary of the breakdown is attached to this presents. “So, Distinguished colleagues, in light of the removal of the critical reforms of my administration, the need to accelerate growth of the national economy provides support for the External Borrowing Plan, which amounts to $20,517,755,901, and €1,045,083,643. ” I want to emphasize that the projects and programs included in the Borrowing Plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country. “These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skilled acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improve the livelihood of the Nigerian child. “The majority of these projects and programs will be implemented across all the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue broader external borrowings to close the financing shortfall. “These funds will primarily be directed towards critical infrastructure projects in various sectors, including power, transportation and healthcare, amongst others. “Given the urgent nature of these needs and the importance of stabilizing the country, it is crucial to seek the consideration and approval of the National Assembly leadership and the entire National Assembly for the 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan. “This will enable the government to fulfill its obligations to the Nigerian people through timely disbursements and effective project implementation. “This request will be looked at by the Committee on Local and Foreign Debts, probably in collaboration with the Preparation and Finance, but majorly by the Committee on Local and Foreign Debts. items.title: « À Contre-Plumes » : Dix auteures font voler en éclats les silences
items.description: Le Salon du livre féminin de Dakar a baissé ses rideaux samedi dernier. Mais cette dernière journée a été l’occasion pour dix auteures de présenter À Contre-Plumes (publié à la maison d'édition Le Fil d'Ariane), le cinquième recueil de nouvelles né de la résidence de création et d’écriture organisée en prélude au Salon. D’un dressing où les chaussures prennent la parole aux rues de Saint-Louis, d’un village du Sahel à un Dakar projeté en 2056, ces nouvelles passent de « l’intime à l’imaginaire, du grave au drôle, du familier à l’inattendu ». L’ambiance est bon enfant et joyeuse à l’occasion de cette séance de présentation. Entre fous rires et étreintes affectueuses, la présentation du recueil collectif, qui a aussi été un moment de retrouvailles, s'est déroulée dans la joie et la bonne humeur. Mais les thématiques abordées par ces dix plumes n’en demeurent pas moins sérieuses. Lire aussi: «À Contre-Plumes», dix voix féminines réunies dans un même recueil À l’image de leurs nationalités multiples, les auteures ont ratissé large. Elles signent des textes aux univers et aux tonalités très différents. Certaines bousculent la forme, d’autres les attentes, mais toutes donnent une place à des personnages qui débordent des cadres, refusent les rôles tout faits ou finissent par s’en écarter. Le recueil s’ouvre sur une allégorie. Dans Entre semelles et lacets, Marie Paul Weecar Tine Basse met en scène des chaussures soumises au « Tri annuel » de leur propriétaire. Sous le registre humoristique, la nouvelle parle de l’impermanence, de la fin d’un cycle et de l’illusion du statut. Escarpina croit que ses origines prestigieuses la protègent, tandis que Derbie, la plus fidèle, finit au sac-poubelle. Fidélité et loyauté ne garantissent rien, et la question finale laisse planer l’idée d’un tri plus définitif, qui rappelle la condition des femmes elles-mêmes. La condition féminine au cœur des récits Cette condition féminine est au cœur de plusieurs textes. Dans Le ciel s’est refermé, Fatoumata Dicko raconte, à travers le regard d’un adolescent peul, la polygamie et la violence silencieuse qu’elle inflige à la première épouse. Le couple modèle formé par ses parents s’effondre sous le poids de la tradition, du Pulaaku, des commérages et de l’injonction faite aux femmes de se montrer patientes et dociles. Maïra se mure dans le mutisme avant de s’éteindre en pleine cérémonie. Dans Mbaa, la douce dissidente, Maimouna Diallo aborde de front les violences conjugales. Elle décrit l’emprise d’un mari qui contrôle les études, les fréquentations et le corps de sa femme, ainsi que son complexe d’infériorité face à une épouse plus instruite. Le tabac, refuge hérité d’une adolescence privée d’affection maternelle, devient finalement le symbole d’une libération. Mbaa porte plainte, obtient son certificat médical et fume ouvertement, savourant « la dissidence ». La mère, entre transmission et deuil Le lien maternel et le deuil traversent également une grande partie du recueil. Pour Christina N’da, son texte n’est pas seulement constitué de mots couchés sur du papier. « Mon objectif était de rendre éternelle une personne qui n’est plus là et qui m’a reliée à la lecture », confie-t-elle à propos de sa nouvelle Allô Maman. À travers ce récit, elle explore la transmission entre trois générations, la maternité vue des deux côtés et les regrets liés à l’éloignement. La chute, ouverte, laisse entendre un souffle au bout du fil. Avec À toi qui m’as tant aimée, Anne-Marie Diédhiou rend hommage à une mère de cœur, sa tante, maman Anna, qui a renoncé au mariage pour élever ses frères avant de l’élever à son tour. « Je rends hommage à une âme extraordinaire qui a occupé une place essentielle dans mon enfance et ma construction », fait-elle savoir. La nouvelle affirme que la maternité est aussi une question de choix, tout en évoquant les traditions diolas, l’exode rural, l’exigence éducative et un deuil qui n’est pas achevé. Dans Amul Yaakaar, Awa Thiongane Gaye prolonge cette figure maternelle avec Ken Bugul, une mère courageuse qui mobilise tout son réseau pour permettre à son fils d’obtenir une bourse. Mais l’amitié est minée par la jalousie : Ousmane, issu d’un milieu aisé, trahit son ami par un simple silence. La pauvreté, les grèves universitaires, le poids d’un prénom qui signifie « sans espoir » et la culpabilité liée à une faute par omission composent un récit de résilience et de secret. Entre science-fiction, censure et liberté D’autres nouvelles tournent le regard vers l’avenir ou vers l’ailleurs. Avec Rougui, Aminata Bocar Ba imagine un Dakar de 2056, à moitié englouti par la montée des eaux, où le monde virtuel éloigne les familles et où un service permet d’envoyer des messages après sa mort. C’est par l’un de ces messages posthumes que Rougui apprend la double vie de son mari, Malick. La nouvelle mêle science-fiction, critique des dérives numériques, crise climatique et illusion d’un mariage parfait, où l’on est « aimée correctement, mais pas exactement ». Dans Bêtes d’encre, Hadassa signe un récit poétique sur l’écriture comme espace de liberté. De l’enfance, où le gribouillage résiste au coloriage, jusqu’à la clandestinité sous un régime autoritaire, Rana et Charbel vivent un amour de toute une vie, nourri de calligraphie et de langues multiples — arabe, latin, amharique et grec. La satire politique, la foi, la transmission de père en fils et la censure débouchent sur une révolution portée par la parole écrite. Quand la parole brise le silence Enfin, deux textes interrogent le pouvoir du silence et de la voix. Soulful, de Fatoumata Koita, suit une jeune femme qui s’attache à un homme jugé fou, dont le journal lui sert de miroir. La nouvelle questionne le regard social sur la maladie mentale, l’exclusion et la solitude, et pose cette question troublante : sommes-nous tous fous ? Sa fin onirique demeure ambiguë. Dans Silence radio, Gaël Hottmongo met en scène Aïcha, animatrice anonyme d’une émission radiophonique destinée aux femmes. Orpheline murée dans le mutisme après une tentative d’infanticide commise par sa propre mère, devenue ministre, elle découvre ses origines et choisit de se montrer à visage découvert. Le texte oppose la force imposée aux femmes à leur droit à la vulnérabilité et célèbre la parole qui soigne, jusqu’à la renaissance et à l’amour retrouvé. Au final, trois fils rouges relient ces nouvelles. Le premier est celui de la condition féminine, avec ses violences, ses injonctions sociales, la polygamie, l’emprise et les sacrifices imposés. Le deuxième est celui du lien à la mère et du deuil, avec ses regrets et sa transmission. Le troisième est celui de la parole contre le silence : écrire, parler, chanter ou fumer en public deviennent autant de gestes de liberté. S’y ajoutent la trahison, le secret et la double vie, qui rappellent que derrière les apparences, chacun et surtout chacune porte un poids que le recueil choisit enfin de mettre en mots. Arame NDIAYE

items.title: Dinar algérien : le dollar poursuit sa hausse, l’euro recule
items.description: Après plusieurs semaines de stabilité, le marché noir des devises en Algérie connaît un regain d’activités. Et c’est le dollar qui en tire profit. Le billet vert se maintient au-dessus de la barre des 240 dinars algériens l’unité et poursuit sa hausse. Pour l’euro, il reste stable, mais sa cote reste toujours élevée. Ce mardi, la monnaie unique européenne est proposée à 276 dinars l’unité et le dollar s’affiche à 242,5 DZD. Par rapport à hier lundi, l’euro a perdu 50 centimes et le dollar a gagné 1,5 dinars. Par rapport à dimanche dernier, la hausse du dollar est encore plus significative puisque la devise américaine était cotée à 240,5 dinars au Square Port-Saïd d’Alger, la plus importante place du marché noir des devises en Algérie. Le 3 octobre, le dollar était à 239,5 dinars et l’euro à 277 DZD l’unité. Dinar algérien : les cours du dollar et de l’euro sur le marché officiel Cette évolution des deux principales devises échangées sur le marché parallèle algérien s’explique par le recul de la monnaie européenne face au dollar sur le marché mondial, mais aussi par la hausse de la demande sur le billet vert de la part notamment des particuliers qui importent des voitures de Chine. Durant les six premiers mois de l’année 2026, les importations algériennes de véhicules de Chine ont dépassé les 190 000 unités ! Sur le marché officiel, le dollar et l’euro restent relativement stables. Le dollar est coté à 134,94 dinars ce mardi contre 134,81 DZD hier lundi. Pour l’euro, il a légèrement augmenté à 150,92 dinars contre 150,89 dinars hier lundi. L’article Dinar algérien : le dollar poursuit sa hausse, l’euro recule est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Agriculture recovery in 2025 was encouraging but uneven, industrial slowdown highlights broader development – ISSER
items.description: Ghana’s agricultural recovery in 2025 was encouraging but uneven, the Institute of Statistical, Social and Economic Research (ISSER) has stated. According to the research institute from the University of Ghana, sustaining growth will require improvements in productivity, market infrastructure and policy implementation. In its 2025 State of the Ghana Economy Report (SGER), ISSER said expanding effective irrigation, mechanisation and extension services, with greater attention to crop yields will raise agricultural productivity. It also pointed out that improving storage, processing, transport and market access to reduce post-harvest losses and improve producer returns will strengthen markets and value chains. It emphasised that agriculture remains central to Ghana’s food security, rural livelihoods and agro-industrial development; therefore, stronger agricultural growth can improve food availability and support economic activity. However, it cautioned that aggregate growth may conceal weaknesses in individual commodities. Industry Sector On the Industry sector, ISSER said Ghana’s industrial slowdown in 2025 highlights the need to translate mineral sector strength into broader industrial development, supported by competitive manufacturing and greater domestic value addition. it alluded that the sector is important for job creation, value addition and economic diversification. It therefore calls for an industry that translates mineral sector strength into broader industrial development, supported by competitive manufacturing and greater domestic value addition On policy priorities, ISSER called for the strengthening of manufacturing competitiveness by reducing production and financing costs, improving infrastructure and supporting investment in value addition. Similarly, it wants improved energy security and efficiency through addressing electricity sector financial and operational weaknesses, strengthening domestic gas supply and expanding renewable energy. Services Sector For the Services sector, the research firm said it is increasingly important for Ghana’s economic growth, employment and structural transformation. In that regard, modern services such as ICT, finance and logistics can raise productivity across the economy, while education and healthcare support human capital development. However, rapid growth in services does not automatically translate into productive employment or better service delivery. It therefore states that quality, accessibility and productivity of services matter as much as their expansion.

items.title: Ils coupent le courant pour braquer une caissière et tombent dans les filets de la BRI
items.description: Une coupure d’électricité provoquée pour neutraliser les caméras de surveillance aurait servi de prélude au braquage d’une caissière à Gagnoa, en Côte d’Ivoire. Deux suspects, un ferronnier de 35 ans et un vigile de 36 ans, ont été interpellés puis déférés devant le parquet. L’information a été rendue publique ce mardi 27 octobre 2026 par la plateforme Police Secours de Côte d’Ivoire. Le braquage aurait été minutieusement préparé. Le jeudi 25 juin 2026, une caissière identifiée par les initiales K.A.S., employée dans une société à Gagnoa, a été victime d’une attaque à main armée sur son lieu de travail. À son arrivée, elle constate une coupure d’électricité et contacte son patron pour lui signaler la situation et solliciter le rechargement du compteur. Alors qu’elle attend le retour du courant, deux hommes font leur apparition dans les locaux. Pensant accueillir des clients, la caissière s’approche de l’un d’eux. Mais ce dernier sort une machette dissimulée sous ses vêtements et la contraint à s’allonger au sol, la menaçant de mort si elle crie. Pendant ce temps, son complice s’empare de l’argent contenu dans la caisse. Environ cinq minutes après leur arrivée, les deux individus prennent la fuite avec un butin de 1 970 000 F CFA, laissant la victime sous le choc. La piste de la coupure électrique Alertée, la Brigade de recherche et d’intervention (BRI) de Gagnoa ouvre une enquête. Les circonstances de la panne électrique survenue juste avant l’attaque retiennent particulièrement l’attention des enquêteurs. Les investigations conduisent à l’interpellation de deux suspects: T.J., un ferronnier de 35 ans, et B.B., un vigile de 36 ans. Au cours de son audition, le ferronnier reconnaît sa participation aux faits et affirme en être l’initiateur. Selon les éléments rapportés par Police Secours, le suspect connaissait déjà les lieux pour y avoir effectué des travaux. Cette expérience lui aurait permis de repérer l’emplacement du compteur électrique ainsi que celui de la caisse. Il aurait ensuite associé son complice au projet criminel. Le jour du braquage, les deux hommes se seraient présentés sur place munis de machettes, avant de couper volontairement l’alimentation électrique afin de neutraliser les caméras de surveillance. La panne signalée par la caissière aurait donc constitué, selon les investigations rapportées, une étape du mode opératoire des présumés braqueurs. Les suspects déférés devant le parquet Malgré les précautions prises, les deux hommes ont finalement été interpellés par les éléments de la BRI de Gagnoa. Au terme de l’enquête, ils ont été déférés devant le parquet près le Tribunal de première instance de Gagnoa pour des faits présumés de vol en réunion avec usage d'armes. Cette affaire rappelle que la connaissance préalable des lieux peut être exploitée à des fins criminelles. À Gagnoa, une coupure de courant présentée comme une simple panne aurait ainsi servi à préparer un braquage, avant que les investigations de la BRI ne permettent de remonter jusqu’aux deux suspects. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Ils coupent le courant pour braquer une caissière et tombent dans les filets de la BRI est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .
