items.title: Le Niger accuse le Tchad d’une frappe meurtrière de drone avec l’appui de la France
items.description: Le gouvernement nigerien a accuse, le 26 octobre, le Tchad d'avoir mene une frappe de drone sur son territoire avec « l'appui de la France ». Dans un communique lu a la television nationale, Niamey condamne un « acte d'agression » et une « violation flagrante » de sa souverainete, tenant N'Djamena pour responsable de l'operation. Selon les autorites nigeriennes, la frappe s'est produite le 24 octobre, vers 1 heure du matin, dans la zone d'Emi Lulu, pres de la passe de Salvador, dans la region d'Agadez. Elle aurait tue deux civils, blesse plusieurs personnes et endommage des vehicules. Situe pres des frontieres algerienne et libyenne, ce secteur minier constitue egalement un passage pour les trafics transfrontaliers. Pour etayer ses accusations, le gouvernement affirme que les investigations menees par les forces de securite et les autorites judiciaires ont permis de reunir des « elements materiels et techniques concordants ». Niamey prevoit de les transmettre aux instances internationales competentes. Leur contenu n'a toutefois pas ete rendu public a ce stade. Le Niger porte l'affaire devant les instances internationales a la suite de cet incident, Niamey a annonce la convocation de l'ambassadeur du Tchad pour lui notifier une protestation officielle. Le gouvernement entend egalement saisir le Conseil de securite de l'ONU et le Conseil de paix et de securite de l'Union africaine. Il reclame une enquete internationale independante afin d'etablir les circonstances de la frappe et les responsabilites eventuelles. Les autorites exigent la cessation immediate des actions qu'elles jugent hostiles et la reparation des prejudices subis. Elles annoncent aussi un renforcement de la surveillance de l'espace aerien et des frontieres. Tout en affirmant ne pas rechercher l'affrontement, Niamey invoque l'article 51 de la Charte de l'ONU, relatif au droit de legitime defense. « La retenue n'est pas la faiblesse », previent le gouvernement. Niamey accuse egalement le Tchad d'offrir un soutien strategique a des mercenaires qui s'en prendraient aux populations et aux infrastructures energetiques nigeriennes. Les autorites inscrivent ces accusations dans une serie d'actions qu'elles imputent a N'Djamena depuis plusieurs mois. La France deja mise en cause dans de precedentes tensions Ces nouvelles accusations surviennent dans un contexte de relations deja degradees. Apres la tentative de mutinerie des 28 et 29 août a Niamey, le capitaine Roger Gabriel avait accuse, debut septembre, des officiers tchadiens d'y avoir participe. N'Djamena avait rejete ces accusations. Les tensions avec Paris s'etaient egalement accentuees. Le 4 septembre, le gouvernement nigerien avait accuse la France d'etre a la tete d'un « vaste reseau de connivences » implique, selon lui, dans une entreprise de destabilisation. a la tribune de l'ONU, le Premier ministre Mahaman Ali Lamine Zeine avait ensuite evoque un projet presume d'attaque aux frontieres du Niger, mettant en cause le Tchad et la France. Le 14 octobre, Niamey avait par ailleurs denonce l'expulsion par Paris de deux de ses agents declares persona non grata . La frappe du 24 octobre constitue ainsi un nouveau sujet de confrontation diplomatique. Ni le Tchad ni la France n'ont officiellement reagi a ces accusations.

items.title: Maresca defends Donnarumma, Guehi after Man City defeat
items.description: Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca on Tuesday defended goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and centre-back Marc Guehi after costly mistakes in their first Premier League defeat of the season at Aston Villa. Nicolas Jackson took advantage of errors from the pair as Villa won 2-1 on Saturday, ending City’s perfect run of seven wins from seven league games. Defeat left City level on points with champions Arsenal at the top of the table, but they are ahead of the Gunners on goal difference. Maresca spoke up for his players ahead of a tough League Cup fourth-round match against Brighton at the Etihad on Wednesday. “Gigio (Donnarumma), I think, since we started, is doing well. Like any player, like any manager, at some point is making some mistakes. “But it’s part of the season. Again, they are playing so many games, so many minutes, that sometimes it’s almost impossible to (not) make some mistakes.” And Maresca said he was “completely happy” with England defender Guehi. “Because in the way he reacts, he’s fantastic, he’s a top guy,” he said. “Again, he’s one of the captains, he’s a leader, and I love Marc, to be honest. “And again, it’s the same with Gigio — when they make some mistakes, they recognise.” Maresca said Donnarumma was among a group of players who had been given time off to recharge after the Villa defeat, also including Erling Haaland, Elliot Anderson, Josko Gvardiol and captain Ruben Dias. “After Villa, we gave five players three days off to recover energy — Erling, Ruben, Elliot, Gigio and Josko,” he said. “They are all on holiday.” AFP The post Maresca defends Donnarumma, Guehi after Man City defeat appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Samuel Jinapor denies Minority coached South Africa evacuees to criticise government
items.description: The Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, has dismissed allegations that the Minority in Parliament attempted to influence Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa to speak against the government. Speaking at a press conference on Tuesday, October 27, Mr Jinapor said the Minority had not offered money or used any form of persuasion to get the returnees to make allegations about the government’s handling of the evacuation and associated allowances. “Let me place on record that at no point in time did the Minority engage, pay, and/or convince any of these people,” he stated. The denial comes a day after some of the evacuees alleged at a press conference that opposition members had tried to coach them to make statements critical of the government. Mr Jinapor said the Minority had not orchestrated the claims, adding that some evacuees had independently spoken out over alleged differences between the amounts they were supposed to receive and the money they actually collected. The controversy has intensified scrutiny of the evacuation exercise, with the Minority questioning aspects of the expenditure and documentation presented in connection with the payments. Among the concerns raised are alleged duplicate entries, unsigned payment records, missing receipts and claims by some returnees that the amounts recorded against their names did not match what they received. Although Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has offered explanations regarding the payments, Mr Jinapor said the concerns warranted an independent examination. He reiterated the Minority’s call for an independent audit to establish whether the evacuation funds were properly accounted for and to resolve the disputed payment claims.

items.title: Las tecnológicas ven ilegales las exigencias del Gobierno a los centros de datos y buscan la vía para tumbar el decreto
items.description: El envío al Consejo de Estado del borrador modificado del Real Decreto sobre los requisitos de acceso y conexión energética para centros de datos ha desencadenado una tormenta en el ecosistema tecnológico. Lo que el Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Ministerio de Transformación Digital ha presentado como una flexibilización del texto original es percibido por la industria como una imposición “inasumible y discriminatoria”. Multinacionales de la talla de Amazon Web Services, Google y Microsoft (en su calidad de hiperescaladores, que son quienes impulsan estas infraestructuras), junto con grandes desarrolladores nacionales como Merlin Properties y ACS, observan con máxima alarma un cambio normativo que, según entienden, amenaza la seguridad jurídica y la llegada de capital extranjero en pleno despliegue de la inteligencia artificial. items.title: Le Moyen-Orient en alerte face à la menace d'une nouvelle offensive israélo-américaine contre l'Iran
items.description: Le spectre d'une nouvelle guerre regionale plane sur le Moyen-Orient. a l'approche des elections legislatives israeliennes du 27 octobre et du scrutin de mi-mandat americain du 3 novembre, les signaux d'une reprise des hostilites contre l'Iran se multiplient. Washington et Tel Aviv auraient elabore des plans pour une campagne de frappes, tandis que Teheran promet une riposte d'une ampleur inedite. Selon un article du New York Times publie le 21 octobre, les etats-Unis et Israel preparent une serie de frappes contre l'Iran, susceptible de viser ses installations nucleaires, ses arsenaux de missiles et ses infrastructures energetiques. ABC News et CNN ont eux aussi rapporte des preparatifs militaires avances. Les etats-Unis renforcent parallelement leur dispositif militaire regional, notamment en deployant des moyens navals et aeriens supplementaires. Le president americain Donald Trump a toutefois affirme le 8 octobre qu'aucune attaque americaine ne serait lancee avant les elections de mi-mandat. Qui prepare la paix prepare la guerre En Israel, la perspective de nouvelles frappes s'invite dans la campagne electorale. Le Premier ministre israelien Benjamin Netanyahou, qui cherche a conserver le pouvoir, fait de la menace iranienne un enjeu securitaire majeur. Des responsables de l'opposition l'accusent neanmoins de vouloir instrumentaliser les tensions militaires a des fins electorales, ce que son entourage dement. L'Iran affirme, de son cote, avoir renforce ses capacites de defense et previent qu'une offensive provoquerait des represailles contre les interets americains dans la region. Les monarchies du Golfe redoutent particulierement des attaques contre leurs installations petrolieres et gazieres. Le detroit d'Ormuz, deja perturbe par les affrontements, demeure un point de tension strategique. Face au risque d'embrasement, plusieurs mediateurs regionaux, notamment le Qatar et le Pakistan, tentent de maintenir un canal diplomatique entre Washington et Teheran. Mais les divergences sur le nucleaire iranien, les sanctions et la liberte de navigation dans le Golfe continuent de bloquer les negociations.

items.title: Kofi Hayford shines as MC of M.anifest’s ‘Nowhere Cool’ at 10 celebration
items.description: Broadcaster Kofi Hayford has earned praise for hosting M.anifest’s 10th anniversary celebration of his acclaimed album Nowhere Cool at the Accra Polo Club on Saturday, 24th October 2026. Known for his eloquence and humour, Kofi kept the concert flowing smoothly, introducing the evening’s opening acts and engaging the audience ahead of the headline performance by the celebrated rapper. His delivery, stage presence and ability to connect with the crowd added to the experience of the Nowhere Cool @ 10 Live Experience , which brought together “M.anifans” to celebrate one of M.anifest’s defining projects. The event featured performances from Kwartengg, Anabel Rose, RCee and Arathejay, who helped set the tone for the night before M.anifest took to the stage. The rapper then performed all 14 songs on the 2016 album, giving fans an opportunity to relive the project in its entirety, a decade after its release. He was joined by a line-up of guest performers, including highlife star Kwabena Kwabena, dancehall musician Samini, Worlasi, Ko-Jo Cue, Ria Boss, Kwarteng, Asiama and Cina Soul. Their appearances added to the excitement of a night built around the music, collaborations and lasting impact of Nowhere Cool . Coverage of the concert also highlighted the audience’s enthusiastic response as M.anifest revisited songs from the album. Kofi’s role was to ensure that the programme maintained its rhythm while giving each performer the right introduction and allowing the audience to remain part of the experience. Rather than allowing transitions between acts to interrupt the mood, he kept proceedings moving and engaged the crowd with intermittent performances of lines from some of the rapper’s most popular records. The young broadcaster also performed as a hypeman alongside DJ Afrolektra during a 20-minute set that saw fans singing along to classic Ghanaian bangers. His performance has since drawn positive reactions from some fans who attended the event, with audiences expressing appreciation for the way he handled his responsibilities on the night. Kofi Hayford told Joy Entertainment that “the assignment was another opportunity to demonstrate the skills that have made me a familiar voice across Ghana’s media and entertainment landscape, and I appreciate the opportunity to serve”. Saturday’s event also marked the second time he had been selected to host an occasion connected to M.anifest. In 2025, he hosted the listening party for the rapper’s NRAGT project in Labone, Accra. His latest assignment further strengthens that association, bringing together his professional experience and personal admiration for an artiste whose music he follows closely. Kofi Hayford is a broadcaster, entertainment journalist, voice-over artiste and experienced event host who has built a career around communication and connecting with people. His work across Joy FM and Joy Prime has given him experience engaging different audiences, from radio listeners and television viewers to live event patrons.

items.title: Congrès électif de la Féguifoot : le ministre des Sports lance un avertissement aux 53 votants
items.description: À l’ouverture de l’Assemblée générale extraordinaire et élective de la Fédération guinéenne de football (FGF), ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, le ministre des Sports, Cellou Baldé, a appelé les membres statutaires à faire primer l’intérêt du football guinéen sur les ambitions individuelles et les rivalités. Il a plaidé pour une gouvernance stable, transparente et résolument tournée vers les résultats. Après une décennie marquée par des crises institutionnelles et des tensions récurrentes au sein de la Fédération guinéenne de football, le ministre estime qu’il est désormais temps de tourner la page des divisions. « Cette situation ne peut plus être considérée comme une fatalité. Il est temps d’y mettre durablement un terme », a-t-il déclaré devant les membres statutaires réunis pour élire la nouvelle équipe dirigeante de l’instance faîtière du football guinéen. Un choix déterminant pour l’avenir du football guinéen S’adressant aux 53 membres statutaires appelés à voter, Cellou Baldé a souligné l’importance de leur responsabilité. Selon lui, le scrutin ne se limite pas à la désignation d’un président et de son équipe. Il engage l’avenir d’une discipline qui suscite la passion de millions de Guinéens. « Quel choix servira le mieux l’avenir du football guinéen ? », a-t-il lancé, invitant les électeurs à privilégier l’intérêt collectif plutôt que les ambitions personnelles et les rivalités. Le ministre a également insisté sur la nécessité d’instaurer une gestion transparente, une administration performante et une culture du résultat. Il a réaffirmé la disponibilité de son département à accompagner la future équipe dirigeante, tout en précisant que cet accompagnement se ferait dans le respect de l’autonomie de la fédération et des exigences de responsabilité. La CAN 2032 ou 2036 en ligne de mire Alors que la Guinée nourrit l’ambition d’organiser la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (CAN) en 2032 ou en 2036, Cellou Baldé estime que cette perspective nécessite des institutions solides et une fédération capable de concevoir et de conduire des projets durables. Pour le ministre, la stabilité institutionnelle et la bonne gouvernance constituent des conditions essentielles pour permettre au football guinéen de franchir un nouveau cap et de concrétiser ses ambitions. En conclusion, Cellou Baldé a rappelé que le football guinéen ne saurait être l’otage d’intérêts particuliers. « Le football guinéen n’appartient à aucun individu, à aucun clan, ni à aucune équipe. Il appartient à la nation et à tous ceux qui le font vivre », a-t-il martelé.

items.title: Fact check: Viral image of Saudi defence minister kissing Iranian president's hand is AI-generated
items.description: Several social media users, including pro-Houthi accounts based on their past posts, have been sharing an image since October 26, on social media platforms Facebook and X, allegedly showing the Saudi defence minister kissing the hand of the Iranian president amid a meeting in Tehran involving the Makkah Defence Alliance. However, the image is old and edited using AI. Iran hosted senior security officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye on Oct 26 for talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. Pezeshkian called for regional unity and a coordinated stance among Islamic countries, urging them to strengthen cooperation and oppose actions by the United States and Israel. The meeting focused on regional security, the consequences of US-Israeli attacks on Iran and efforts to de-escalate tensions. Iranian officials said the four countries agreed to continue talks on regional peace and security, while Saudi Arabia said the visit aimed to promote dialogue and support mediation efforts by Qatar and Pakistan. On Oct 26, a Houthi supporter, based on their past posts, shared an image on X allegedly showing Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman kissing the hand of the Iranian president. The post gained 63,000 views. A pro-PTI user also shared the same image in a similar context with the following caption: “In fact, this is the path to peace. Come to Tehran and pledge allegiance. Welcome, my beloved.” The post attracted 27,000 views on X. Several other pro-Houthi accounts further reposted the same image on Facebook and X, as seen here , here , here , here , here and here. A keyword search was conducted to determine whether any credible Saudi, Iranian, or international media outlets had published the image or reported on an incident in which the Saudi defence minister allegedly kissed the Iranian president’s hand, but yielded no reports. Investigating the image also found several visual discrepancies, such as deformities around the Saudi official’s fingers and hand as he kisses the Iranian president’s hand. There were also slight deformities and distortions on the Iranian president’s cheek and neck as well, hinting that the image was likely edited through AI. The image was then analysed using multiple AI-detection tools to assess whether it had been artificially generated or manipulated. Hive Detect reported a 99 per cent likelihood of AI generation, while DeepAI and TruthScan also indicated a 90pc likelihood that the image was edited using AI. A reverse image search of the viral photo yielded an Arab News report covering the funeral procession of assassinated Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on July 3, 2026. The report stated that Saudi Deputy Foreign Minister Waleed El Khereiji attended the ceremony, where he met Iranian officials, including President Masoud Pezeshkian. The featured image in the Arab News report shows a strong resemblance to the viral photo, with the same background and the officials wearing similar attire. However, a comparison of the two images reveals a key difference. The viral image depicts the Saudi official kissing the Iranian president’s hand, whereas the original image shows him simply shaking hands with the president. The same report, featuring the same image, was also published by Saudi news outlet Saudi Gazette and the official Saudi Press Agency . Therefore, the claim that a viral image shows the Saudi defence minister kissing the hand of the Iranian president is false. The image is edited using AI, and the older original picture does not even feature the Saudi defence minister. This fact check was originally published by iVerify Pakistan — a project of CEJ-IBA and UNDP.

items.title: Resign, support Obi, KNN replies RMRDC boss
items.description: .Challenges Shettima to explain subsidy savings, rising debt By Steve Oko The Kwankwaso National Network, KNN, has challenged the Director-General of the Raw Materials Research and Development Council, RMRDC, Prof. Nnanyelugo Ike-Muonso, to resign his appointment and support the presidential ambition of his kinsman, Mr Peter Obi, rather than campaign for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election based on selfish interests. KNN’s reaction followed Ike-Muonso’s recent call on Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, to drop his ambition and support Tinubu in 2027, arguing that the South should complete its eight-year tenure before power returns to the North. The group, a support network for Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, described the position as disappointing, arguing that Nigeria needed leadership capable of addressing economic hardship, unemployment, insecurity and declining purchasing power rather than continuity with policies it blamed for the country’s difficulties. KNN sought to know how Obi’s emergence as Nigeria’s President in 2027 would disadvantage the South as claimed by Ike-Muonso, asking whether Obi is a Northerner. The group argued that Obi who had declared his intention to be in office for only one term if elected, will only be completing the turn of the South. KNN in a statement by its South East Regional Coordinator, Dr Ukpai Iro Ukpai, said the 2027 election should be about competence, accountability and national recovery, not merely regional power rotation. “2027 is not about the continuation of misgovernance and ineptitude; it is about rescuing Nigeria from total collapse,” the group declared. It described Obi as a credible alternative with national appeal across ethnic and religious divides, urging Nigerians dissatisfied with the current administration to support his presidential project. KNN also criticised Vice President Kashim Shettima over his reported remark that Obi had nothing to offer beyond statistics. Shettima made the comment at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit, where he questioned Obi’s economic proposals and his opposition to the restoration of petrol subsidy. Challenging the Vice President, KNN said he should counter Obi’s figures with verifiable data rather than make sweeping allegations. The group also demanded explanations for the administration’s borrowing despite its claims of increased fiscal savings following petrol subsidy removal in May 2023. It challenged Shettima to provide a transparent account of the savings generated, how the funds had been deployed and the tangible benefits Nigerians had received. KNN further questioned the progress made in rehabilitating Nigeria’s state-owned refineries, demanding clarity on expenditure, operational capacity and timelines for delivering results. The group argued that Nigerians deserved measurable improvements in living standards, energy security and economic opportunities rather than repeated assurances of recovery. It warned that political rhetoric would not shield the All Progressives Congress, APC, from electoral rejection if the government failed to address citizens’ concerns. KNN maintained that the 2027 election should be determined by candidates’ competence, policy proposals and performance, insisting that Nigerians deserved accountability and a government that prioritised their welfare. The post Resign, support Obi, KNN replies RMRDC boss appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Niger Miners’ deaths: Panel details roles of NSCDC commandant and four officers
items.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The independent ministerial committee probing the deaths of miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) has detailed the alleged roles of the suspended Niger State Commandant, Suberu Aniviye, and four other officers in the incident. The committee accused the officials of various acts of misconduct, including unlawful detention, failure to respond to distress signals, poor supervision and attempts to alter the detention facility before an independent forensic examination. The committee’s chairman, Jonathan Kure, presented the report to the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, in Abuja on Tuesday. In its findings, the panel said Aniviye authorised and supervised the operation without adequate planning, approval or oversight, permitted overcrowding and failed to ensure that detainees were held in accordance with lawful procedures. “The committee found extensive failures of leadership, supervision and professional conduct. State Commandant Suberu Aniviye authorised and supervised the operation without proper planning, approval or oversight,” Kure said. “He permitted overcrowding, failed to ensure lawful detention practices and later issued a false public statement attributing the deaths to a disease outbreak. The committee concluded that his actions reflected gross leadership failure, abuse of authority and serious professional misconduct.” The committee identified CSC Oluwadare Sunday, head of the Investigation Unit, as another officer whose actions contributed to the failures. It said he facilitated unlawful detention practices, disregarded legal and medical concerns and failed to intervene despite knowing that conditions in the detention facility were deteriorating. SC Usman Isah Ndamaka was accused of maintaining overcrowded conditions and instructing subordinates not to open the cell. According to the panel, he also failed to respond appropriately to emergency alerts and participated in cleaning and altering the detention area before independent investigators examined it. The committee further faulted Station Guard ASCI Hassan Mohammed for allegedly failing to open the cell despite repeated distress signals and not adequately escalating the emergency. Another officer, DSC Sule Garba, was accused of profiling detainees, including minors, without adequately protecting their rights. The panel also said he failed to properly document exhibits. DSC Musa Marafa was accused of unlawfully arresting and detaining one Emmanuel Emeka over a civil death dispute. The committee said his actions contributed to Emeka’s continued detention until his death alongside other detainees. Beyond the conduct of the individual officers, the committee identified broader institutional shortcomings within the NSCDC, including inadequate detention facilities, weak custodial oversight, the absence of closed-circuit television monitoring, poor record-keeping and insufficient emergency medical capacity. Other deficiencies listed in the report included ineffective supervision, weak intelligence reporting arrangements, workforce imbalance and chronic underfunding. The panel warned that these weaknesses created conditions in which serious violations could occur without timely detection or intervention. The committee said the investigation also faced challenges that limited aspects of the forensic assessment. It said the detention register for September 16, 2026, was unavailable, while 30 of the 33 deceased persons had been buried before post-mortem examinations could be conducted. It added that the detention area had been cleaned, disinfected and altered before independent forensic investigators arrived, affecting aspects of the examination. The post Niger Miners’ deaths: Panel details roles of NSCDC commandant and four officers appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Burkina/Commerce international : Les opérateurs économiques sensibilisés aux conditions de voyage et au règlement des différends commerciaux
items.description: La Chambre de commerce et d'industrie du Burkina Faso (CCI-BF), avec l'accompagnement du ministère de l'Industrie, du commerce et de l'artisanat et du ministère des Affaires étrangères, organise, ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou, une session d'information à l'intention des opérateurs économiques. Cette initiative vise à renforcer leurs connaissances sur les conditions de voyage à l'international et les mécanismes de prévention et de règlement des différends commerciaux. Les opérateurs économiques burkinabè entretiennent de nombreuses relations d'affaires avec des partenaires étrangers, notamment dans le cadre des opérations d'importation et d'exportation. Toutefois, ces échanges comportent des risques qui peuvent compromettre leurs activités. Paiements non effectués, marchandises non livrées ou non conformes, contrats insuffisamment encadrés et difficultés d'obtention de visas figurent parmi les problèmes régulièrement rencontrés. Les sessions s'adressent principalement aux opérateurs économiques burkinabè engagés dans des relations d'affaires à l'international. Elles sont également ouvertes à toute personne ou institution intéressée par les thématiques abordées C'est pour contribuer à la prévention de ces situations que la CCI-BF a initié cette session d'information. Les échanges sont organisés autour de deux panels consacrés à la gestion des relations d'affaires à l'international et aux mécanismes de règlement des conflits commerciaux. Les communications portent notamment sur les précautions à prendre avant la conclusion d'un partenariat, les clauses essentielles des contrats commerciaux, les instruments de paiement et les voies de recours en cas de litige. Les participants sont également informés des conditions d'entrée et de séjour dans certains pays partenaires, notamment la Chine, l'Inde et la Turquie. À l'issue de chaque session, un rapport de synthèse sera élaboré. Il présentera les principales difficultés rencontrées par les opérateurs économiques ainsi que les recommandations adressées au secteur privé, à la CCI-BF et aux ministères concernés Prévenir les risques liés aux transactions internationales Pour le directeur général adjoint en charge des infrastructures et du développement au sein de la CCI-BF, Fousséni Koné, cette initiative répond aux préoccupations exprimées par les entreprises burkinabè à travers le dispositif d'écoute et d'appui-conseil de l'institution. Il a indiqué que les difficultés rencontrées dans les échanges commerciaux internationaux peuvent entraîner des pertes financières importantes, des retards dans les activités et, dans certains cas, fragiliser durablement les entreprises. « Dans les affaires à l'international, la confiance est indispensable, mais elle ne saurait remplacer la vigilance. La réussite d'une opération commerciale repose aussi sur la qualité des vérifications préalables, la clarté des engagements contractuels, la maîtrise des moyens de paiement et la connaissance des règles applicables dans le pays partenaire », a souligné Fousséni Koné. Fousséni Koné a remercié les ministères chargés du commerce et des affaires étrangères, les représentations diplomatiques, les experts et les équipes ayant contribué à l'organisation de cette session Il a également rappelé que la CCI-BF a pour mission d'accompagner les entreprises, de défendre leurs intérêts et de rechercher, avec les acteurs concernés, des solutions aux difficultés qui entravent leurs activités. Présent à cette session, le conseiller technique du ministre de l'industrie, du commerce et de l'artisanat, Seydou Ilboudo, a réaffirmé l'engagement du gouvernement à accompagner les entreprises burkinabè dans leur ouverture aux marchés internationaux. Il a relevé que plusieurs litiges résultent notamment de l'absence de contrats suffisamment solides, de la méconnaissance des instruments de paiement internationaux et du manque de vérification de la crédibilité des partenaires commerciaux. À ces difficultés s'ajoutent les pratiques frauduleuses dont certains opérateurs économiques sont victimes. « Ces réalités ne doivent pas constituer un frein à l'accès de nos opérateurs économiques aux marchés extérieurs, car mieux ils sont informés, mieux ils sauront se prémunir des risques liés au commerce international », a déclaré Seydou Ilboudo. Seydou Ilboudo a salué l'initiative de la CCI-BF, qui vise à renforcer les connaissances des opérateurs économiques sur les risques liés au commerce international Le conseiller technique a par ailleurs salué la participation des banques, des assurances, des institutions chargées du règlement des litiges, des acteurs de la justice commerciale, des partenaires diplomatiques et des experts. Il a assuré que le ministère chargé du commerce accordera une attention particulière aux recommandations formulées à l'issue des différentes sessions. Une initiative saluée par les opérateurs économiques Du côté des participants, cette session suscite de l'intérêt. Pour l'un d'entre eux, Léon Nikiema, elle répond à une attente du secteur privé, confronté à des difficultés dans l'accomplissement des formalités de voyage et la gestion des différends commerciaux avec des partenaires étrangers. Il estime que certains commerçants ne disposent pas de suffisamment d'informations sur les conditions d'obtention des visas commerciaux et les règles applicables lors de leurs déplacements professionnels. « Il est essentiel que les autorités compétentes, notamment le ministère chargé du commerce et la Chambre de commerce et d'industrie du Burkina Faso, renforcent l'information et la sensibilisation des acteurs du secteur privé. Leur accompagnement est également nécessaire pour faciliter la résolution des différends rencontrés à l'international », a souhaité Léon Nikiema. Léon Nikiema a assuré que les informations recueillies au cours de cette session seront partagées avec les autres membres des faîtières professionnelles d'hommes et de femmes d'affaires Le participant a également insisté sur la nécessité de faire parvenir les informations aux commerçants qui n'ont pas pu prendre part à cette session. À cet effet, il invite les responsables d'associations et de faîtières professionnelles présents à organiser des séances de restitution au profit de leurs membres. Cette session de Ouagadougou s'inscrit dans un programme de sensibilisation qui prévoit quatre étapes, respectivement à Ouagadougou, Bobo-Dioulasso, Koudougou et Ouahigouya. À travers cette tournée, la CCI-BF et ses partenaires entendent permettre à un plus grand nombre d'opérateurs économiques de mieux sécuriser leurs transactions internationales et de prendre les précautions nécessaires lors de leurs voyages d'affaires. Samirah Bationo Lefaso.net

items.title: UPSA Banking and Finance students learn to prepare wills as part of financial literacy drive
items.description: Level 400 Banking and Finance students at the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), have been guided to write their first wills as part of efforts to promote early estate planning and responsible wealth management among young people. The practical exercise formed part of the fifth National Estate and Gift Planning Awareness Conference (NEGPACON 2026), organised by the Centre for Financial Literacy Education Africa (CFLE Africa) in collaboration with the UPSA Faculty of Accounting and Finance. The conference sought to raise awareness of estate planning, succession, wills, and estate and gift tax considerations. Facilitated by lawyer Benjamin Kodwo Agyare, the session introduced students to the practical steps involved in preparing a will, including identifying assets, selecting beneficiaries and clearly stating their wishes. The exercise was designed to help students apply their classroom knowledge to real-life financial decisions and challenge the perception that wills are only necessary for older people or those with substantial wealth. Financial literacy must include wealth transfer Executive Director of CFLE Africa, Peter Asare Nyarko, said financial literacy education should go beyond earning, saving and investing to include protecting and transferring wealth. “We want young people to understand that building wealth is only one part of the journey. They must also understand how that wealth can be protected, preserved and transferred responsibly,” he said. According to him, introducing university students to wills and succession planning would help them develop responsible financial habits early in life. He added that knowledge of estate planning was particularly important for Banking and Finance students, who could eventually work with individuals and families on financial management and wealth preservation. Mr Agyare said the practical approach helped students understand that preparing a will was not exclusively for wealthy or elderly people. The session also highlighted the need to review estate plans as personal circumstances change, including through marriage, having children, acquiring property and establishing businesses. Students welcome practical experience President of the Banking and Finance Students Association, Josephine Gyekyewaah, said the exercise had changed her perception of wills and estate planning. “Before this session, I think many of us saw wills as something for older people or people who already have a lot of property. But going through the process ourselves changed that perspective. It made me realise that estate planning is about being intentional and responsible with whatever you have,” she said. Student participant Ampofo Bright Ntow said the exercise encouraged him to reflect on his assets and how they should be distributed. “The session made me think about the things I already have and the things I hope to acquire in the future. I had never seriously thought about who would benefit from my assets or what would happen to them if I was no longer around,” he said. He added that writing a will made the subject easier to understand by allowing students to consider the decisions involved rather than simply learning about them in theory. Another participant, James Laryea, said the workshop had demonstrated that people did not need to accumulate substantial wealth before considering estate planning. “One of my biggest takeaways is that you don’t have to wait until you have millions of cedis before you start planning. What matters is that you begin to take responsibility for what you have,” he said. He noted that preparing a will provided an opportunity for individuals to communicate their wishes and reduce uncertainty over their assets. Preparing future financial professionals The initiative forms part of efforts to broaden financial education by incorporating succession planning, inheritance and wealth preservation into the training of future financial professionals. Organisers say early exposure to estate planning can help students develop a more comprehensive understanding of personal and family financial management. Through NEGPACON, CFLE Africa is promoting an approach to financial literacy that covers not only wealth creation but also its protection, preservation and responsible transfer. For the participating students, the exercise provided an opportunity to reflect on their present assets, future financial goals and the importance of making informed decisions about their estates.

items.description: Sri Lanka stormed into the final of the One-day International tri-series after overwhelming Pakistan by eight wickets, chasing a modest target of 111 in just 18.1 overs at the Gaddafi Stadium on Tuesday. Left-arm pacer Dilshan Madushanka delivered a career-best five for 34 to dismantle Pakistan for 110 in 25.3 overs before Kamindu Mendis struck an unbeaten 62 to guide Sri Lanka to 114-2, sealing victory with 31.5 overs to spare. The result confirmed Sri Lanka’s place in Saturday’s final alongside Pakistan, who had already qualified after winning their first three matches. England’s remaining league fixture against Sri Lanka on Thursday consequently became a dead rubber. Pakistan’s batting collapsed against a disciplined Sri Lankan attack after captain Kusal Mendis won the toss and elected to field. The hosts struggled to cope with Madushanka’s short-pitched deliveries and never recovered from losing wickets at regular intervals. Babar Azam top-scored with 29 off 33 balls, including five boundaries, while Hasan Nawaz made 17. Captain Shaheen Shah Afridi contributed 15 off 13 deliveries, striking two sixes in a late attempt to lift the total. Pakistan lost Fakhar Zaman for five in the fourth over when he mistimed a short delivery from Madushanka and was caught at point. Maaz Sadaqat, making his first appearance in the tri-series after being added to the squad a day earlier, managed eight before Asitha Fernando trapped him leg-before with a yorker. Saad Baig fell for five, caught at short cover off Madushanka, while Salman Ali Agha made nine before edging Sahan Arachchige behind. Pakistan were 61-4 when Babar was trapped leg-before by Eshan Malinga for 29, having already lost their two reviews. The collapse gathered pace as Arachchige dismissed Shadab Khan for two and Dunith Wellalage removed Hasan Nawaz, who was caught by Arachchige for 17. Pakistan slumped to 91-8, leaving the lower order with too much to do. Madushanka returned to claim the remaining wickets, dismissing Arafat Minhas for 10 and Haris Rauf for one before ending the innings with Shaheen’s wicket. The Pakistan captain’s brief counterattack included two sixes, but he was caught by Wellalage as Madushanka completed his five-wicket haul. Arachchige took two wickets, while Asitha, Malinga and Wellalage claimed one apiece. Sri Lanka’s reply began aggressively, with Kamindu and Avishka Fernando putting on 50 for the opening wicket in 6.5 overs. Avishka struck two fours in his 17-ball 16 before pulling Shaheen to Fakhar at short midwicket. Kamindu, however, continued to score freely, reaching his half-century off 43 balls. He survived a dropped catch in Shaheen’s opening over and successfully reviewed an lbw decision before going on to finish unbeaten on 62 from 60 deliveries, with eight fours and two sixes. Pakistan briefly found another breakthrough when Kusal, who had struck two boundaries in his six-ball eight, was bowled by Arafat for 8. The dismissal came in unusual fashion, as the ball ricocheted off the batter’s bat and into the stumps. But the hosts could not build on the wicket. Pavan Rathnayake joined Kamindu and remained unbeaten on 23 off 26 balls, striking two fours as the pair guided Sri Lanka home without further loss. Kamindu’s fluent innings ensured the chase remained firmly under control, while Rathnayake finished the contest by driving Maaz’s spin through cover-point for four. Shaheen and Arafat took one wicket each, but Pakistan’s total left their bowlers with little margin for error. Sri Lanka completed a comprehensive victory that capped a strong turnaround in the tournament, with their batters having also impressed in their earlier win over England. For Pakistan, the defeat exposed familiar top-order weaknesses after their dramatic one-wicket victory over England on Sunday. Shadab’s unbeaten century had rescued that match, but this time the batting line-up failed to provide a competitive total. Madushanka’s outstanding spell proved decisive, giving Sri Lanka the momentum to secure qualification and setting up a final against Pakistan on Saturday.

items.title: Ronaldo in line for Portugal return after fallout with coach
items.description: Cristiano Ronaldo is in Portugal’s preliminary squad for next month’s Nations League matches, opening the door to an international return after his fallout with coach Jorge Jesus, a federation source told AFP on Tuesday. The 41-year-old abruptly left the Portugal camp on September 30 during the opening qualifiers for the Nations League, before accusing Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time. A spokesperson for the Portuguese football federation (FPF) confirmed reports Ronaldo was in line for a return to the squad ahead of games at home to Denmark and in Wales on November 14 and 17. Jesus will announce his final squad on November 6, the spokesperson added. The FPF last week announced it had handed Ronaldo a 30-day suspension for walking out. The suspension was backdated, meaning he will be free to return by the end of this week. Ronaldo apologised to supporters earlier in October, adding he would accept any punishment that was imposed. In a social media post shortly after deserting his teammates, he accused Jesus of promising to give him playing time against Norway before failing to honour it but insisted he was not retiring from international duty. He said a further bone of contention between him and the coach was Jesus had not mentioned at a press conference prior to the game with Denmark a series of points they had agreed upon. Reigning champions Portugal won all four of their Nations League matches, three of them without Ronaldo, and qualified for the quarter-finals with two games to spare. The five-time Ballon d’Or winner is the all-time top goalscorer and record appearance-maker in men’s international football. Ronaldo, who made his Portugal debut in 2003 at the age of 18, has said this will “probably” be his final year in football. tsc/jde/mw/pi The post Ronaldo in line for Portugal return after fallout with coach appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ballon d’Or win ‘feels like a dream’, says Kane as tributes pour in
items.description: Harry Kane said Tuesday that his Ballon d’Or triumph “feels like a dream” as tributes poured in for the first English winner of the award in a generation. The England and Bayern Munich forward fended off competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to be named the world’s best men’s footballer at the London Palladium theatre late on Monday. Wembley was lit up to recognise Kane’s achievement, with England’s X account carrying the message: “The home of the world’s best footballer.” The former Tottenham forward is the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001. The 33-year-old struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double. The England captain, who also picked up the men’s striker of the year award, scored six times as his side finished third at the World Cup in North America. “It sounds crazy to be honest but it sounds pretty good,” Kane told Sky Sports on Tuesday. “What a special night. An incredible feeling. I’m still just trying to take it all in really. It feels really, really like a dream. “The emotion (when his name was called) was relief, joy, happiness, excitement. There was so much waiting to find out the winner and in that moment it was quite nerve-wracking so to have that kind of release and to be able to share it with everyone there in that theatre was special.” Prince William, patron of the Football Association, praised the England skipper. “What a fantastic achievement and so deserved,” he wrote on Instagram. “A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments.” – Superlatives – England boss Thomas Tuchel, who was Bayern boss when Kane arrived in Germany in 2023, said the Three Lions were “lucky” to have him as their leader. “I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I’m delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world,” he said. “To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader.” England and Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice described Kane as “incredible” while Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers, another international teammate, said he was the “best ever”. Bayern Munich president Herbert Hainer said the award was “a proud day for FC Bayern”. “Harry Kane can do it all –- and he scores goals, goals and more goals. He now joins a line with Franz Beckenbauer, Gerd Muller and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge (as previous Ballon d’Or winners) –- that says everything about our history,” he said. “The club and Harry Kane have got together, grown together and achieved the highest aims together. We are proud that this all-round outstanding sportsman and person is part of our FC Bayern family.” Harry Redknapp, former Tottenham manager, described his all-round game as “brilliant”. “It isn’t just his goalscoring that is good, it is his all-round play, and the way he is and the way he is around the players. He is great as the England captain,” he told the BBC. “No one could have deserved this more, it has been a brilliant story.” AFP The post Ballon d’Or win ‘feels like a dream’, says Kane as tributes pour in appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: “Advertising Brings a Player Once, Actually Paying Winners Brings Them Back” — Helabet Representative Says
items.description: Nigerian iGaming sector has undergone a seismic shift over the past eighteen months following the Supreme Court’s late-2024 ruling that decentralised the industry and secured state-level regulatory authority. In this interview with Yusuf Lawal , Helabet representative Olajay discusses how the company is handling the regulatory chaos, shares a few internal user-growth figures, outlines plans for advertising strategy changes, and even explores the possibility of sponsoring a Nigerian football club. Your company has been in Nigeria for a while now. How big is Helabet in 2026? By our internal figures, we had 2.5 million active users by the third quarter of 2025. That’s a hard number from our player database audit — [shows a smartphone screenshot of the dashboard to showcase the number and the relevant description that proves it, but concealing the rest of the data] — but it is not for publishing; I can only share it like that, sorry. We have probably added a few hundred thousand since then. But I won’t make assumptions a couple of months before the upcoming annual audit. And besides, raw numbers don’t matter that much to us. We are even pivoting our advertising strategy towards spending less. And this has already attracted more players than during our usual marketing campaigns. A bold statement, considering Nigeria is one of Africa’s most competitive betting markets and other operators are fighting tooth and nail for every bit of visibility. Care to explain? Visibility still matters, yes. Not going to pretend ads do nothing; they bring impressions and let Nigerian players know Helabet exists. But the economy is not the same as six or even two years ago. Just an example that dozens of millions of my compatriots can relate to: in September 2019, $1 was ₦360. In September 2026, $1 costs around ₦1,325. The exchange rate has dropped by 3.7 times. And while today the local player wagers more in naira than in 2019, in $ the growth does not compensate for this drop. But a lot of CAC operations [Customer Acquisition Cost, total expenses needed to attract a new customer] are tied to the $. Marketing costs more in $ in 2026 than in post-COVID-19 2021, when we were just starting in Nigeria. Some channels became too expensive due to increasing competition or rising compliance costs. Others became irrelevant due to legal changes and, again, compliance. You do not even need to dig into staff and digital infrastructure support costs to see that burning money in the budget race is an unsustainable strategy, even short-term. When these changes were only looming, we asked ourselves a simple question: what does advertising actually buy? It brings a player to Helabet once. How long they stay depends on the product, payouts, rewards and support. A positive gaming experience, paying winners on time and solving their problems builds our brand reputation and reduces churn [percentage of players who stop depositing and betting over a specific time period, usually measured in periods between 7 and 90 days] . Fail their trust — and funds invested in CAC are gone with your reputation. Helabet is all about building trust by giving players exactly what we promised during sign-up. This is the policy we have entered the Nigerian iGaming market with. Or any other African market we operate in. But in the new circumstances, we chose to double down on this policy. And redirected even more money from marketing into customer experience assets: bonuses, localisation, our team, payouts… Oh yes, Nigerian bettors have some very public arguments about not getting their winnings. How are you going to tackle this growing lack of trust towards sportsbooks? This might sound new to some, but often sportsbooks withhold payments because they lack sufficient operational balance to suddenly pay out a large single win or a volume of winning bets placed on a high-odds event. And they fail to notice that even a single complaint going viral over tens of thousands on social media from a customer denied their legitimate funds will destroy their previous marketing investments. And trust. So continuing to build and protect trust with our players by paying out winnings on time is our best bet, pun intended. That is why part of our funds went into operational balance. So any bettor at Helabet could be assured that if they legitimately win a large sum, they will promptly receive their money upon request. But paying winners is a bookmaker’s basic obligation. Should that really be counted as a competitive advantage? It should be basic. But reality bites. The local betting industry is at a stage where players compare sportsbooks based on whether they trust the payout to happen or not. Open any betting discussion on social media, and it is all complaints about delayed and missing payments, frozen accounts. There is even an ongoing case of ₦900 million in unpaid winnings. I will not call names because everyone already knows who you are. The best Helabet can do is lead by example, showing everyone that giving more value back to players is a better way of doing things than giving them more ads to watch. For example, thanks to the budget redistribution, we are planning to get player attention with a new 305% Helabet welcome bonus package. A 305% bonus will definitely get attention from Nigerian players. But how are you planning to fit this into your existing bonus system? The new 305% welcome bonus is just our first handshake with the player; we’ve just made it twice as powerful as the previous one and are currently in the TOP 3 in Nigeria by welcome bonus size. The aim is to help the player get into the game and give them more chances. But our system is more than that and features a 25% daily bonus on top of the first deposit of the day, a weekly rebate and another new feature, the Promo Code store, where players can exchange bonus points for single and accumulator bets. And remember I mentioned us shifting more to localisation as well? We also have a very local bonus just for Nigeria: free internet data for MTN and Glo users. A noticeable part of our current and potential player base is on metered mobile data packages, and the cost of the package affects their player experience. So Helabet designed this bonus around the unique Nigerian reality; we do not have such a bonus in other African countries where we operate. Where else does Helabet operate? And how is Nigeria that different from the other markets? I am in touch with local Helabet teams operating in English-speaking Africa: Kenya, Tanzania and Ghana. This is our philosophy — local execution everywhere. Local offices, local employees. I strongly believe that you cannot run an ambitious company in any African country from another continent. The payment systems, regulatory framework, average bet size, preferred leagues and sports — I can confirm that the true experience of managing all this in a single product comes from living and working here. My homeland is potentially the largest betting market in Africa, with 240 million people. And things here can get very chaotic very fast. At the end of 2024, the iGaming regulation was decentralised, and the states received authority over it. This raised an issue for us of how to remain compliant everywhere in Nigeria, when there was no more unified licence to obtain. Luckily, the establishment of FSGRN [the Federation of State Gaming Regulators of Nigeria] spared us the hassle of obtaining 37 licences, one for each state and a separate one for FCA. Helabet obtained a URC [Universal Reciprocity Certificate], acting as a unified licence valid across all 22 member states. There was also a strong year-long pushback and related uncertainty via an attempt to pass the Central Gaming Bill 2025, until our president, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, decided not to assent to it in December 2025. No way a non-Nigerian remote team could handle this the proper way we did, and it makes me proud. But currently, we are adjusting to the recent Nigeria Tax Act 2025. This game never ends. Kind of a headache to navigate this every day with due diligence, especially when some of your competitors are known to be “cutting corners”? Staying compliant requires diligence, absolutely. But Helabet won’t compromise on its compliance policy. And as a Nigerian, I fully support this. If you want to call yourself a local Nigerian betting brand, you must be a responsible participant in the Nigerian economy, not a revenue extractor. This means working with state regulators and paying your taxes. Even if offshore brands outpace you in revenue in the short term, the iGaming sector will get more and more regulated each year; this is a global trend. So a better strategy is to embrace it and contribute to the local economy instead of “cutting corners” and taking the risks. And as a Nigerian, I would add that if you want Nigerian players but none of the Nigerian obligations, I don’t think you can seriously call yourself a local brand. If you are putting down local roots, what is Helabet ultimate endgame in the Nigerian market? We want to be the sportsbook Nigerians recommend to their friends because they are genuinely happy with odds, event selection, bonuses and withdrawal of winnings. Become the most trusted operator on the market. And since my team is all-Nigerian, we are extra-driven to achieve this not just for the sake of Helabet, but also to improve our iGaming sector and country as a whole. This is a bit of an insider reveal, but we are considering becoming a sponsor of a Nigerian football club. We already have a shortlist of local clubs and will open negotiations in due time. Personally, I think this is a very responsible move — to contribute to local sports, rather than just profit from the public passion for it. Thank you for the interview. Any words of conclusion? Just a message to the Nigerian iGaming industry as a whole. Go local. Obtain a licence if you haven’t already. Hire and train Nigerians motivated to change the industry for the better. Build digital expertise. Pay taxes that apply to you. Invest in local sports. The sportsbooks that will successfully survive into the next decade will be all about that. Official sites: helabet.ng helabet.com The post “Advertising Brings a Player Once, Actually Paying Winners Brings Them Back” — Helabet Representative Says appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CAN to DSS, Police: Probe video threatening Christians, prosecute culprits
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) has urged the Department of State Services (DSS), the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to investigate a viral video showing a young man leading boys in chants threatening attacks on Christians in Enugu and Jos during Sunday worship, demanding that those responsible be brought to justice. The association warned that the threats must not be dismissed as mere chants, insisting that Nigerians must be free to gather for worship without fear of being attacked because of their religious beliefs. In a statement by its President, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, CAN condemned the apparent incitement to religious violence, expressing particular concern over the involvement of children and young persons in the threatening chants. “The possibility that young people are being exposed to or encouraged to embrace such hatred raises serious concerns that must not be ignored,” Archbishop Okoh said. CAN urged security agencies to establish when and where the video was recorded, identify those involved and determine who organised or facilitated the activity. It also called for an assessment of potential security risks and adequate protection for Christian communities and places of worship in Enugu, Jos and other parts of the country. While acknowledging the reported disavowal of the video by the leadership of Jama’atu Izalatil Bid’ah Wa Iqamatis Sunnah (JIBWIS), the association insisted that the denial should not take the place of an independent investigation. “The denial of responsibility by any organisation cannot replace an independent investigation into the identities of those involved, the origin of the video and the circumstances surrounding the chants,” it said. The association further urged investigators to establish whether any individuals or groups sponsored, encouraged or facilitated the threats, insisting that anyone found culpable must face the law without favour or discrimination. CAN also called on religious leaders to reject any teaching or activity that promotes hatred or violence against people of other faiths, warning against exposing young Nigerians to messages that portray fellow citizens as enemies because of their religious beliefs. It cautioned that failure to act could embolden those who threaten citizens on religious grounds and further undermine peaceful coexistence in a country already grappling with violence and deep-seated distrust. “Allowing such conduct to go unchallenged would send a dangerous message that threats against citizens on religious grounds can be made without consequence,” the association said. CAN urged Christians to remain calm, vigilant and law-abiding while the investigation proceeds, warning against retaliatory actions that could put lives at risk and deepen religious divisions. The association reaffirmed its commitment to religious freedom, justice and peaceful coexistence, insisting that every Nigerian was entitled to equal protection under the law, regardless of faith. It charged the government to move beyond condemnation, establish the facts and hold those responsible accountable, warning that the safety of citizens and their freedom to worship must not be left at the mercy of religious extremists. items.title: At least 1 killed, 6 injured as roof of under-construction building collapses in Multan
items.description: LAHORE: At least one individual was killed, while six others were injured on Tuesday when the roof of an under-construction building collapsed near Multan’s Northern Bypass, Rescue 1122 said. In a statement, the rescue service said the roof of an under-construction plaza had collapsed near the National College of Business Administration and Economics on Northern Bypass. The agency said that so far, six injured individuals had been rescued and shifted to Nishtar Hospital, adding that one person was killed in the collapse. Rescue officials launch a search and rescue operation after building collapse in Multan on October 27, 2026. — Photo via Rescue 1122 A rescue operation was underway to rescue trapped individuals, Rescue 1122 said, adding that at least 10 to 15 labourers were working at the site at the time of the incident. Upon receiving the information, Rescue 1122 relief teams were immediately dispatched to the incident site, the statement said. “Rescue 1122 teams reached the incident site within three minutes and initiated the search and rescue operation,” it said. The statement said 10 vehicles were actively engaged in the relief operations. The relief operations include five ambulances, three rescue motorbikes, one rescue vehicle, and one fire vehicle, it added. Rescue officials launch a search and rescue operation after building collapse in Multan on October 27, 2026. — Photo via Rescue 1122 In a statement, a spokesperson for Nishtar Hospital said that six injured were shifted to the hospital, adding that the hospital record showed that another individual was brought dead. As per the records, three injured received head injuries — whose nature and criticality are unknown — while the other three received minor injuries. The spokesperson said doctors and paramedical staff were on high alert in the emergency room, and the best medical facilities were being provided to the injured. Building and roof collapses are common in Pakistan, often attributed to poor safety standards and the use of substandard construction materials. A teacher and 30 students were killed when a school’s roof collapsed in Peshawar earlier this month. In September, two men died in Pakpattan after the roof of their house collapsed during heavy rain and a windstorm. On June 30, 14 children lost their lives when the roof of a private tuition centre collapsed in Lahore’s Kahna area.

items.title: Six times English players won Ballon d’Or
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Harry Kane has joined an exclusive group of English footballers to have won the prestigious Ballon d’Or, becoming the fifth Englishman to claim the men’s award after his remarkable 2025/26 campaign with Bayern Munich and England. The England captain scored 73 goals for club and country last season, ending a 25-year wait for an English winner following Michael Owen’s triumph in 2001. Here are the English players who have won the Ballon d’Or and the years they claimed football’s prestigious individual honour. Sir Stanley Matthews (1956) The legendary Blackpool winger became the first-ever Ballon d’Or winner when he received the award in 1956. Known for his exceptional dribbling skills and ability to beat defenders, Matthews made history at the age of 41, a record that still makes him the oldest winner of the award. Sir Bobby Charlton (1966) Charlton won the Ballon d’Or in the same year England lifted their first and only FIFA World Cup title. The Manchester United legend played a key role in the Three Lions’ triumph on home soil, scoring three goals during the tournament, including two in the semi-final victory over Portugal. Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) Keegan became the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or in consecutive years. He claimed the award in 1978 and retained it in 1979 while playing for German side Hamburg. His performances in Germany established him as one of the leading footballers of his generation. Michael Owen (2001) Owen became the fourth Englishman to win the award after an outstanding year with Liverpool. He helped the club secure the FA Cup, League Cup and UEFA Cup in the 2000/01 season, scoring crucial goals along the way. His speed, finishing and memorable performances for club and country helped him beat the competition for the award. Harry Kane (2026) Kane became the fifth Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or after an extraordinary season with Bayern Munich and England. His 73 goals across 65 appearances helped Bayern win the Bundesliga, DFB Pokal and Franz Beckenbauer Supercup. He also helped England finish third at the 2026 World Cup, their best result since winning the tournament in 1966. Kane’s triumph ended the long wait for another English winner and placed him alongside some of the biggest names in the country’s football history. A record worth noting: Although five Englishmen have won the award, Kevin Keegan remains the only English player to have won it twice in consecutive years. Kane is the latest addition to a list that stretches back seven decades. Vanguard News The post Six times English players won Ballon d’Or appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Immersion patriotique obligatoire: le film «Serment d’une génération» présenté au public
items.description: Le réalisateur, Boubié Richard Tiéné, a projeté, son film documentaire intitulé: «Immersion patriotique obligatoire: Serment d’une génération», au public, lors d’un avant-première, ce lundi 26 octobre 202026, à Ouagadougou, au centre culturel du Faso, ex-Canal Olympia Ouaga 2000. A travers ce film de 90 minutes, le journaliste Tiéné, plonge les cinéphiles au cœur de la formation civique et physique visant à renforcer le patriotisme des nouveaux bacheliers. Dans le cadre de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP) lancée le 1er avril 2025 par le chef de l'Etat burkinabè, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, les plus hautes autorités du pays, dans la dynamique de redynamiser la flamme patriotique, ont initié l'Immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO). Pour déconstruire les préjugés entourant cette vision, le journaliste et réalisateur, Boubié Richard Tiéné, a réalisé un film documentaire de 90 minutes. Une vue des appelés Ce lundi 26 octobre 2026, le long-métrage a été projeté en avant-première au public au centre culturel du Faso, ex-Canal Olympia Ouaga 2000. Présenté en présence des autorités, dont le ministre d'Etat, ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, le général Célestin Simporé, l'œuvre évoque le vécu des 30 jours des immigrés lors de leur aventure à l'occasion de l'Immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO). A travers ce film documentaire, Richard Tiéné montre non seulement la ferveur populaire qui accompagne l'IPO, précisément dans les différentes localités où pendant un mois, son équipe de tournage a séjourné, mais également, les moments de larmes et de rires qui caractérisent la formation. Le réalisateur, de par ce documentaire, vise aussi à rassurer les parents des nouveaux bacheliers sur les conditions réfléchies pour offrir un meilleur encadrement des appelés à l'IPO. Le réalisateur du film documentaire, Richard Tiéné «C’était important d’immortaliser ce moment pour rassurer les parents que quand leurs enfants vont à l’immersion patriotique, ce n’est pas une prison. Il y a une vie et ils sont à une autre école d’éducation», a expliqué Boubié Richard Tiéné. «Quand vous regardez le film, vous comprenez que (la) santé des (appelés) est prise en charge», a-t-il soutenu. Le général de Division, Célestin Simporé, ministre d'Etat, ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, était présent à la cérémonie en tant que représentant du chef du gouvernement. Après avoir apprécié l'œuvre de belle facture, il a salué le grand travail abattu par le Richard Tiéné et son équipe. Le ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique a indiqué que cette production participe de la conservation de la mémoire nationale. Une vue du public Pour le général Célestin Simporé, l’IPO constitue une base solide pour l’avenir du pays des « Hommes intègres » conformément à la vision du président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré qui veut une jeunesse très bien formée. Le ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique a appelé les jeunes à s'approprier les concepts de souveraineté et en faire leur guide pour servir la nation. A ce propos, il a invité la jeunesse à se former, à être disciplinée et surtout à avoir l'amour de leur patrie. Par Bernard BOUGOUM L’article Immersion patriotique obligatoire: le film «Serment d’une génération» présenté au public est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Économie russe : jusqu’à quand Moscou peut-il financer la guerre contre l’Ukraine ?
items.description: Dans son projet de budget pour 2027, le gouvernement russe prévoit de consacrer 35 % de ses dépenses à la défense nationale, qui finance l’essentiel de la guerre en Ukraine. Au total, les dépenses de défense devraient atteindre 17 100 milliards de roubles (soit environ 190 milliards d’euros), ce qui représente le triple du budget des armées françaises pour 2027 (63,4 milliards d’euros). Il n’est pas certain que le Kremlin puisse financer durablement un tel niveau de dépenses. Celles-ci seront en partie financées par la dette : le ministère des Finances prévoit d’émettre 7 700 milliards de roubles (85 milliards d’euros) d’obligations, contre 5 400 milliards (60 milliards d’euros) dans le budget de l’année dernière. Malgré une hausse de la TVA en janvier 2026 et la création de nouvelles taxes, ces dépenses devraient s’accompagner d’un déficit plus élevé que prévu : 5 500 milliards de roubles (60 milliards d’euros, 2,2 % du PIB) en 2027, contre 3 200 milliards (35 milliards d’euros) dans le budget de l’année dernière. Dans le même temps, Moscou peine de plus en plus à trouver preneur pour sa dette. Le ministère des Finances a dû déclarer infructueuses des adjudications d’obligations en juillet puis en septembre, faute d’offres à un prix acceptable Russia Has No More Money to Throw at Its War in Ukraine. Its 2027 Budget Shows Why », United24 Media , 23 octobre 2026.'> 1 . Entre-temps, les émissions ont été suspendues pendant plusieurs semaines. Afin d’attirer des acheteurs, le gouvernement russe doit offrir des rendements de près de 17 % : le 14 octobre, il a emprunté à 16,77 %, soit son taux le plus élevé depuis février 2025. La demande repose de plus en plus sur les grandes banques, qui ont acheté le 2 septembre 84 % d’une émission de 1 000 milliards de roubles, après avoir emprunté la veille un montant quasi équivalent auprès de la Banque centrale Пушки без масла. Кто заплатит за войну в 2027 году , Carnegie Politika, 29 septembre 2026.'> 2 . La stratégie ukrainienne de frappes à moyenne et longue portée en Russie accroît la pression sur le Kremlin. Le 1er septembre, Poutine a déclaré que les frappes ukrainiennes en mer Noire et en mer d’Azov visant des navires et des infrastructures énergétiques auraient provoqué des dégâts représentant « environ 1 % du PIB » russe, soit environ 23 milliards d’euros. Les frappes ukrainiennes se sont poursuivies depuis et ont notamment visé des centres de données de Yandex, qui soutiennent l’économie civile russe (recherche en ligne, taxis, livraisons, services de messagerie, cloud…). Certains de ces centres de données abritent des supercalculateurs parmi les plus puissants du pays selon TOP500, comme Galouchkine, hébergé dans le centre de données de Vladimir. L’entreprise affirme que ces supercalculateurs, qui permettent de faire tourner l’IA de Yandex, utilisée dans l’ensemble des logiciels et applications de l’entreprise, n’ont pas été endommagés par les frappes . Ils ont toutefois été « transférés vers de nouveaux sites », selon le service de presse de Yandex Яндекс » рассказал о состоянии суперкомпьютеров после атак на ЦОДы », RBC , 26 octobre 2026.'> 3 . La fragilité du budget russe tient aussi à l’imprévisibilité inhérente à la guerre : les dépenses pour renforcer les capacités anti-drones, remplacer du matériel ou payer les primes d’engagement aux combattants dépendront de l’évolution des équilibres sur le front. L’article Économie russe : jusqu’à quand Moscou peut-il financer la guerre contre l’Ukraine ? est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Congrès électif de la Feguifoot : « le pays est fatigué des crises à répétition », le cri d’alarme de Blasco Barry
items.description: L’Assemblée générale extraordinaire et élective de la Fédération guinéenne de football (FGF) s’est ouverte ce mardi 27 octobre 2026 à Conakry, dans un contexte marqué par des crises institutionnelles à répétition. À l’ouverture des travaux, le secrétaire général de l’instance, Ibrahima Blasco Barry, a lancé un appel à l’apaisement, à l’unité et au strict respect des textes régissant le football guinéen. Dans son discours, le responsable administratif n’a pas occulté les difficultés auxquelles la Fédération a été confrontée, notamment les divergences internes et les interprétations contradictoires de certaines dispositions statutaires. « Notre pays est fatigué de voir les crises se répéter, les divisions se prolonger et les énergies qui devraient être consacrées au développement du football être absorbées par des conflits internes », a-t-il déclaré. Pour Ibrahima Blasco Barry, il est désormais essentiel de faire prévaloir l’intérêt supérieur de l’institution sur les intérêts individuels et les ambitions personnelles. Un principe qu’il a résumé en rappelant que les dirigeants et les mandats sont appelés à se succéder, tandis que l’institution, elle, doit perdurer. « Les dirigeants passent, les mandats passent, les générations passent, l’institution demeure », a-t-il souligné. Au-delà de l’enjeu électoral, le secrétaire général de la FGF espère que cette assemblée permettra de restaurer la confiance entre les différents acteurs et de jeter les bases d’une gouvernance plus stable, au service du développement du football guinéen. Dans cette perspective, il a insisté sur la nécessité de dépasser les clivages pour préserver la cohésion au sein de la famille du football guinéen. « La Fédération guinéenne de football ne doit pas avoir des vainqueurs et des vaincus, elle doit avoir une seule famille du football guinéen », a-t-il conclu. Reste désormais à savoir si cet appel à l’unité sera suivi d’effets. Les futurs dirigeants de la FGF sont attendus sur leur capacité à traduire ces engagements en actes concrets, dans un environnement où les crises institutionnelles ont trop souvent détourné les énergies des véritables enjeux : la structuration et le développement du football guinéen.

items.title: UK to charge varsities $1,200 per Nigerian, other foreign student from 2028
items.description: …Targets $594m revenue in first year By Nkiruka Nnorom & Marvellous Chukwunenye Universities in England will now have to pay an annual levy of £925 ($1,200) for each international student beyond an exemption threshold from August 2028, in a move targeting institutions enrolling students from Nigeria, China, Pakistan, India and Bangladesh. The policy, first announced in the UK government’s 2025 budget, was reaffirmed by the Education Minister, Josh MacAlister, who asserted that the revenue would support England’s higher education and skills system. The fresh levy, according to the Department of Education, covers both new and existing students. MacAlister noted that the government had conducted consultations and published an impact assessment in 2025, with an updated analysis expected shortly. He maintained that a planned increase in domestic tuition fee caps could generate about £6 billion for providers over five years, compared with the levy’s projected cost of less than £1 billion. Under the proposal, universities will pay £925 annually for each international student, with the first 220 overseas enrolments exempted. The Office for Students will oversee implementation using enrolment data. Government projects the levy will generate £445 million ($594 million) in 2028-2029, with the figure rising to £480 million ($641 million) by 2030-2031. Home Office figures showed that Nigeria received 26,060 sponsored study visas in the year ending June 2026, behind China with 86,368 and India with 82,523. Pakistan recorded 19,600, while Bangladesh got about 8,800. For Nigerian students, who form one of UK’s largest international cohorts, the charge could translate to higher tuition. The Department for Education data further showed that Nigerian students generated £1.7 billion in UK higher education export revenue in 2024, compared with £5.3 billion from India and £4.9 billion from China. Overall, international students generated an estimated £23.9 billion. Birmingham City University has already raised fees for continuing international students by 2 per cent for 2026-2027, with further 3.5 per cent planned for 2027-2028. The University of Bath has advised overseas students who began in 2026 to budget for annual increases of up to 8 per cent. Meanwhile, some British universities had withdrawn admission offers to Nigerian, Pakistani and Bangladeshi applicants over concerns of breaching stricter visa sponsorship requirements.
