items.title: Surpopulation carcérale en RDC : l’ASADHO et la FBCP appellent à une réforme du système pénitentiaire
Gadi Eisenkot, le général d'origine marocaine qui veut faire tomber Netanyahou
items.description: Sobre dans ses apparitions publiques, peu démonstratif et adepte des discours structurés en points brefs, Gadi Eisenkot cultive une image à rebours de celle de Benyamin Netanyahou. À 66 ans, cet ancien chef d’état-major de l’armée israélienne entend battre le premier ministre sortant lors des prochaines élections. Les sondages annoncent une compétition serrée entre les deux hommes. Pour une partie de l’électorat, la réserve d’Eisenkot, dont le style porte la marque de sa culture militaire, constitue précisément l’un de ses principaux atouts. Là où Netanyahou, qui détient le record de longévité à la tête du gouvernement israélien, maîtrise parfaitement l’anglais avec un accent américain et multiplie les déclarations spectaculaires devant les médias américains ou sur les réseaux sociaux, Eisenkot peine à s’exprimer dans cette langue. Il privilégie une posture modeste et sérieuse, loin de la communication flamboyante de son rival. Cette différence de tempérament ne traduit toutefois pas nécessairement une opposition de fond sur les questions politiques. À la tête de l’armée israélienne de 2015 à 2019, Eisenkot promet de réunifier une société profondément divisée après les années Netanyahou, durant lesquelles l’extrême droite a élargi sa base de soutien. Son discours répond à une aspiration à l’apaisement, estime Tal Elovitch, du centre de recherche Molad. « En Israël, une large partie de la population n’a qu’un objectif principal pour les prochaines élections : que les choses se calment, tout simplement », observe-t-il. « La classe moyenne cherche quelqu’un qui semble capable d’assumer ses responsabilités et qui soit ennuyeux. Je pense qu’Eisenkot correspond à ce profil », ajoute le chercheur. L’ancien chef d’état-major entend également restaurer l’image internationale d’Israël, dégradée par trois années de guerre dans la bande de Gaza et par les violences en Cisjordanie occupée. Il promet de sévir contre les colons qui s’en prennent aux Palestiniens sans être sanctionnés. Des colons ont récemment agressé une journaliste américaine et un maire français. Eisenkot a qualifié ces actes de « terrorisme juif », qu’il attribue à la politique du gouvernement Netanyahou. Une ligne dure sur la question palestinienne L’image d’un candidat soucieux d’apaisement ne doit cependant pas être confondue avec celle d’un partisan de la paix. Eisenkot a lui-même cherché à concurrencer Netanyahou sur son terrain, en direction de l’électorat de droite, en s’engageant à ne jamais autoriser la création d’un État palestinien. Pour étayer sa position, il a diffusé une vidéo datant d’une précédente période politique, dans laquelle le premier ministre actuel, soumis à des pressions américaines, se déclarait ouvert à cette possibilité. Son parcours militaire témoigne également d’une conception particulièrement dure de l’usage de la force. Pendant la guerre de 2006 contre le Hezbollah, alors qu’il dirigeait l’armée, Eisenkot a élaboré la doctrine dite de la « Dahiyé », du nom de la banlieue sud de Beyrouth, bastion du mouvement chiite. Celle-ci préconise le recours à une force disproportionnée contre les infrastructures civiles dans les zones où les groupes armés bénéficient d’un soutien local. Israël a de nouveau appliqué cette doctrine dans la bande de Gaza, où les destructions ont atteint une ampleur telle que des détracteurs estiment qu’elles sont constitutives de crimes de guerre. Les origines marocaines, un ressort électoral La trajectoire personnelle d’Eisenkot contribue aussi à façonner son image. La mort de son fils, Gal, et de deux de ses neveux au cours des combats à Gaza lui a valu une large sympathie dans l’opinion publique. Ses origines populaires constituent un autre élément de son attractivité électorale. En cas de victoire, il deviendrait le premier premier ministre israélien juif séfarade, issu de communautés dont les racines se trouvent au Moyen-Orient et en Afrique du Nord. À l'inverse de Netanyahou, issu d’une famille d’élite dont le père était un universitaire de renom aux États-Unis, Eisenkot est le fils de Juifs marocains. Il a grandi dans les périphéries et les régions reculées d’Israël. Cette origine sociale a été propulsée au cœur du débat politique après les propos d’un commentateur influent de la chaîne 14, favorable à Netanyahou. Celui-ci a qualifié Eisenkot de « singe » manipulé par « l’élite ashkénaze », désignant ainsi les Juifs d’origine européenne qui ont historiquement dominé les institutions politiques et économiques israéliennes. En hébreu, le terme employé ne constitue pas nécessairement une insulte à caractère ethnique : il peut également désigner un « bouc émissaire », chargé de porter la responsabilité des autres. La déclaration a néanmoins provoqué une vague de condamnations, émanant de responsables de l’opposition comme de Netanyahou lui-même. Eisenkot n’a pas tardé à exploiter cette controverse. Son équipe de campagne a fait afficher des slogans dénonçant les discriminations visant les Séfarades. Son parti a, parallèlement, accusé Netanyahou de marginaliser les membres du Likoud issus des communautés juives orientales, en limitant leurs apparitions médiatiques pendant la campagne. Des promesses pour séduire des électorats opposés Au cours de ses interventions publiques du week-end, Eisenkot s’est employé à toucher des catégories d’électeurs aux attentes parfois contradictoires. Dans un café branché, lors d’un forum consacré à la communauté LGBT+, il a promis de renforcer les protections dont bénéficient ses membres. Il a ensuite rencontré des juifs religieux, devant lesquels il a défendu le maintien du contrôle israélien sur la Cisjordanie. Dimanche, s’adressant à des représentants du mouvement du sionisme religieux, il a affirmé que la colonisation israélienne en Cisjordanie « a de la valeur à condition qu’elle serve les intérêts de l’État d’Israël et qu’elle soit menée conformément à la loi ». Cette formulation semble marquer une opposition aux avant-postes sauvages, construits sans autorisation, qui ont contribué à alimenter la récente recrudescence des violences contre les Palestiniens. Sur le front de Gaza, Eisenkot s’est engagé à mettre fin au pouvoir du Hamas dans un délai de dix-huit mois. La semaine dernière, il a exposé deux voies possibles pour atteindre cet objectif : l’application du plan de cessez-le-feu présenté par le président américain, Donald Trump, qui prévoit un désarmement progressif du Hamas et un transfert du pouvoir, ou le recours à des « opérations militaires innovantes » visant à détruire la branche armée du mouvement. L’ancien chef d’état-major s’est également saisi d’un autre sujet particulièrement sensible en Israël après trois années de guerre : les exemptions de service militaire accordées aux étudiants des écoles religieuses. Il promet de les réduire et de faire adopter une « loi sur le service national universel », qui obligerait les juifs ultraorthodoxes, les « haredim » , ainsi que les citoyens arabes, à effectuer un service militaire ou civil. Dans le même temps, il cherche à rassurer les électeurs centristes et libéraux. Il s’engage à « protéger l’indépendance de la justice, l’État de droit, les droits des minorités et la liberté de la presse ». « Israël a besoin de changement » La campagne d’Eisenkot repose ainsi sur une équation délicate : incarner une rupture avec le style et la gouvernance de Netanyahou sans renoncer aux positions sécuritaires susceptibles de rassurer la droite israélienne. Son profil d’ancien militaire, sa réserve et ses origines marocaines lui permettent de se présenter comme une alternative, tout en défendant une ligne ferme sur la question palestinienne et la sécurité d’Israël. Lors de son dernier grand meeting électoral, il a directement interpellé les électeurs de Netanyahou qui hésitent encore à lui renouveler leur soutien, les appelant à modifier leur choix dans les urnes. « Au fond de vous, vous savez, vous aussi, qu’Israël ne peut pas continuer ainsi », leur a-t-il lancé. Avant de conclure : « Israël a besoin de changement ». items.title: Bayern praise ‘humble’ Kane after Ballon d’Or win
items.description: Bayern Munich assistant coach Aaron Danks on Tuesday praised Harry Kane after his Ballon d’Or win, saying the striker will already be focused on scoring his “next goal”. Kane, 33, was awarded the prestigious honour in his hometown of London on Monday evening, breaking through to win the award for the first time. Englishman Danks, who is in the dugout while head coach Vincent Kompany recovers in hospital from a virus, said receiving the game’s highest individual award would not change the England captain’s mindset. “I’m really happy for him and proud of what he’s achieved. I know Harry and his full focus will now be on his next goal, his next performances, his next games,” Danks said at a press conference on Tuesday. “He’ll be straight back into that professional, humble mindset that got him to this level.” Kane had won several goalscoring honours and was runner-up in the Premier League and Champions League with Tottenham but did not break through for a first team trophy until after he moved to Bayern in 2023. Since arriving in Munich, Kane has won two Bundesliga titles and the German Cup, along with making the Champions League semi-finals in two of three seasons at Bayern. Danks said the former Spurs striker was finally getting the recognition he deserves. “I remember years ago when he was back home in England and everybody spoke about him not winning trophies, but if you looked at his career and what he was achieving, he was having a fantastic career. “He was taking the England team to European finals, he was taking Tottenham to Champions League finals. “Maybe he wasn’t getting the recognition in terms of trophies that he deserved, but those things are coming now for him.” Kane and the remaining Bayern contingent who went to London for the ceremony will return to Munich later on Tuesday ahead of Wednesday’s German Cup match against second-tier Magdeburg. “They’re due back at lunchtime today. He’ll train, practice this afternoon and be available for tomorrow… Our full focus is on the game tomorrow,” Danks said. Danks also said he had visited Kompany in hospital and revealed the manager, who was rushed to hospital on Friday after collapsing on the training pitch, was improving. “He’s in good spirits. It looks like every day he’s getting better. There’s no major updates in terms of diagnosis or a return to work, it’s very calm, let him rest, let him recover.” After seven games, Bayern sit top of the Bundesliga, level on points but ahead on goal difference from Borussia Dortmund, with the two sides facing off in Munich on Saturday. items.title: Minority demands Ablakwa’s resignation or dismissal over SA evacuation payments
items.description: The Minority in Parliament has called on Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa to resign over allegations that some Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa received less than the GH¢5,500 support package announced by the government. They want the President to sack him if he fails to resign. The demand was made by the Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, at a press conference at Parliament on Tuesday, October 27. Mr Jinapor also called for a comprehensive independent audit of the evacuation exercise by an internationally reputable accounting firm to establish the facts surrounding the alleged payment shortfalls. “Given the gravity of these revelations and in order to ensure an impartial investigation into the matter, we call on the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Honourable Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, to resign immediately. His handling of this exercise has brought his high office into disrepute,” he said. He argued that the Minister must accept responsibility in line with Section 2.1(j) of President John Dramani Mahama’s 2025 Code of Conduct and Ethics for Political Appointees, which he said requires resignation where a Minister’s actions or leadership result in significant failure, corruption or a breach of public trust. Mr Jinapor further called on President Mahama to terminate Mr Ablakwa’s appointment if he refuses to resign, citing Article 81(a) of the 1992 Constitution. “The President must demonstrate that the standards he has set for his appointees have consequences when public confidence in their stewardship has been seriously undermined,” he added. The demand follows reports that at least three people contacted from the evacuation list claimed they received GH¢2,000 instead of the GH¢5,500 announced by the government. However, Mr Ablakwa has denied the allegations, insisting that all Ghanaians on the evacuation list, including minors, received the full package comprising GH¢5,000 in reintegration support and GH¢500 for transportation. Speaking to the Ghanaian community in Ottawa, Canada, during an official working visit, the Minister said his ministry had received no complaints about payment shortfalls since the evacuation exercise began more than four months ago. He also maintained that no concerns were raised at the airport over missing envelopes or payments below the announced amount.

items.title: At UNGA debate, Pakistan warns against adding more permanent members to Security Council, extending veto privileges
items.description: Pakistan has warned that adding more permanent members to the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) and extending veto privileges would “deepen existing inequalities, perpetuate historical advantages and increase the risk of Council paralysis”. The counsellor at the Pakistan Mission at UN, Gul Qaiser Sarwani, presented these views at the UN General Assembly during a debate on the use of the veto. He said Pakistan called for “comprehensive, democratic and equitable reform of the UN Security Council” and stressed that the misuse of veto power undermined UNSC’s effectiveness, weakened the credibility of the UN and perpetuated inequalities within the international system. “Strategic rivalries and narrow interests among the Council’s permanent members had repeatedly impeded collective action on international peace and security,” he said, emphasising the “unique legitimacy” of the UNGA, whose universal membership and democratic decision-making enabled it to respond when the UNSC unable to act, including due to the exercise of the veto. The Pakistani delegate opposed the creation of any new permanent seats in an expanded Security Council. On proposals to regulate the use of the veto, he said Pakistan favoured its abolition or, at a minimum, severe restrictions on its use. He emphasised that the veto must not be expanded and reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for General Assembly resolution 76/262, which provides for a UNGA debate following the exercise of a veto to promote greater accountability. Sarwani stressed that any measures to restrain the veto must remain consistent with the UN Charter. He called for a balanced approach combining restrictions on veto use with enhanced representation and a stronger role for elected members of the UNSC, making its decision-making “more democratic and providing an effective check on the exercise of veto power”. The delegate further emphasised that the question of the veto must be addressed alongside the other four interrelated clusters under the Intergovernmental Negotiations on Security Council reform, as part of a comprehensive reform package. Concluding his remarks, he reiterated “Pakistan’s strong commitment to reform that corrects existing imbalances, strengthens accountability and serves the collective interests of the entire UN membership rather than a select few”. “Reform for all. Privilege for None!” he said. A recent UN report has also warned that the veto power of the five permanent members of the Security Council is one of the reasons multilateral mechanisms have been unable to prevent or stop the growing number of state-based conflicts. The resulting paralysis has weakened decision-making processes, prompting the UN secretary general to call for Security Council reforms, including an expansion of its membership to ensure fairer representation, particularly for Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, and the Asia-Pacific region, it says. “All these voices are underrepresented despite bearing much of the burden of peacemaking in an increasingly multipolar world,” the ‘World Social Report 2026’ notes.

items.title: Lina Attalah in custody after court issues LE3 mn fine, orders Mada Masr’s closure
items.description: Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah was fined LE3 million by the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, which convicted her on charges of managing an unlicensed website, issuing an order for the website’s closure. Attalah was taken into custody after the issue of the ruling. Tuesday’s session at the ninth circuit of the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, presided over by judge Mohamed Mubarak, was temporarily suspended for deliberations after Attalah’s defense counsel requested time to review the case file. After the court returned from deliberations, the judge ordered the courtroom cleared of everyone except Attalah and her defense counsel, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights’ executive director Hossam Bahgat, who was also present, told Mada Masr. The room then filled with plainclothes officers and guards, with a National Security Agency officer in attendance, he added. The presiding judge and a Supreme State Security Prosecution representative returned to the session and the judge announced that the court has decided to stand by its rejection of all the procedural arguments presented by the defense, including requests to bring in any documentation or hear any witnesses. The judge then asked the defense team to present its plea. The counsel insisted that it would not submit a plea as long as its requests were unanswered by the court. The judge then abruptly asked for a lawyer unknown to any member of the defense counsel to be brought in, “in a move that astonished all those present,” said Bahgat, and announced that the court decided to appoint a lawyer for Attalah. At that point, all members of the defense counsel cried out to reject the court’s appointment of a lawyer when the eight chosen lawyers were present. Attalah herself spoke to say she did not accept the court-appointed lawyer acting on her behalf, an objection the judge refused to have recorded in the session’s minutes. “In an even more shocking move,” said Bahgat, the judge himself began to log down the requests of the court-appointed lawyer, without the lawyer having said a word. The judge then read out the conviction amid shouts and protests from the defense counsel. The judge sentenced Attalah to the maximum possible penalty: a LE3 million fine, the closure of Mada Masr’s website and the confiscation of its property. Security personnel then surrounded Attalah, lifted her off the ground and took her out of the courtroom, where she remains in custody in the courthouse. items.title: Obuasi SHTS sexual abuse allegations should not define secondary education – Haruna Iddrisu
items.description: Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu has urged the public not to generalise about Ghana’s second-cycle education based on the sexual misconduct allegations at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS). He said the incident should not be used to judge the standards, discipline and performance of senior high schools across the country. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Tuesday, October 27, Mr Iddrisu maintained that secondary education in Ghana continued to uphold discipline and established standards, despite the concerns raised by the allegations. “Let us not use the Obuasi incident to stereotype. There is everything good and well with secondary education in Ghana; there is discipline, students and teachers are keeping to the rules and standards across the country,” he said. His comments come amid public concern over allegations of sexual misconduct involving the headmaster of Obuasi SHTS, which have prompted calls for accountability and investigations into the circumstances surrounding the case. Mr Iddrisu urged the public to assess the wider secondary education sector on its overall performance rather than allowing a single case to shape perceptions of schools nationwide.

items.title: Ouagadougou : New Tech Burkina offre une voie éclairée de 1 km aux populations des arrondissements 3 et 9
items.description: L’entreprise New Tech Burkina S.A.R.L a procédé le vendredi 23 Octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, à la remise officielle d’une voie réhabilitée reliant les arrondissements 3 et 9 de Ouagadougou. Longue de plus d’un kilomètre et équipée de 50 lampadaires solaires, cette voie située dans le secteur 38, a été aménagée à hauteur de 12 millions de francs CFA, au profit des populations riveraines. Autrefois réputée criminogène et difficilement praticable, cette voie bénéficie désormais d’un éclairage public grâce à l’installation d’une cinquantaine de lampadaires solaires répartis de part et d’autre. Un aménagement qui devrait permettre aux riverains de regagner leurs domiciles dans de meilleures conditions de sécurité. La voie est désormais réhabilitée et électrifiée Spécialisée dans les nouvelles technologies de l’information et de la communication, l’entreprise New Tech Burkina S.A.R.L est à l’origine de cette initiative. Selon Jean-Pierre Zoungrana, représentant du directeur général de l’entreprise, la voie menant à Tampouy était auparavant impraticable. Il s’est ainsi dit satisfait de l’aboutissement des travaux, qui contribueront à améliorer les conditions de déplacement des populations. Le représentant du DG de New Tech Burkina SARL, Jean Pierre Zoungrana « C’est avec une grande fierté que nous posons cet acte-là. Il contribue au bien-être des populations de la zone et au rayonnement de la RPP » a-t-il indiqué. Jean-Pierre Zoungrana a également précisé que des lampadaires ont été installés sur la voie passant par Jeanne d’Arc ainsi que dans le sous-quartier, particulièrement dans la section 623. PDS de l'arrondissement 9, Jocelyne Traoré/Sanon Présentes à la cérémonie de réception, les autorités administratives, coutumières et religieuses, ainsi que les représentants de la veille citoyenne ont salué cette action patriotique. La présidente de la délégation spéciale de l’arrondissement 9, Jocelyne Traoré/Sanon, a notamment salué une initiative qui s’inscrit dans la dynamique de l’appel lancé par le chef de l’État invitant chaque Burkinabè et chaque entité à jouer sa partition dans la construction d’un Burkina Faso nouveau, souverain et prospère. Christine Ilboudo, Riveraine Christine Ilboudo, riveraine, s’est réjouie de cette initiative qui vient répondre à une préoccupation des habitants. « C’est une voie qui est vraiment fréquentée et avec l’éclairage public, je pense que nous allons réduire considérablement les tensions criminelles et vraiment assurer un déplacement sécurisé à nos populations » a-t-elle déclaré. À travers cette initiative, New Tech Burkina S.A.R.L réaffirme son engagement citoyen et sa volonté de contribuer au développement du Burkina Faso. Un acte patriotique qui témoigne de la responsabilité sociale de l’entreprise et de sa détermination à accompagner les efforts des autorités pour l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations. Sidziguin Irène Corinne SAWADOGO Minute.bf

items.title: Mbappé face au Ballon d’Or : quand le génie du football dérange les puissants
items.description: Le football moderne a-t-il encore la capacité de reconnaître librement ses légendes, ou est-il devenu prisonnier d’un système où les intérêts économiques, les stratégies médiatiques et les jeux d’influence prennent progressivement le pas sur le mérite sportif ? Si j’avais un seul conseil à donner à Kylian Mbappé, ce serait celui-ci : ne participe plus à cette grande représentation médiatique qu’est devenue, à mes yeux, la cérémonie du Ballon d’Or. Kylian, tu es plus grand que ce théâtre. Plus grand que ces cercles d’influence où se croisent technocrates, financiers, dirigeants et faiseurs d’opinion, qui semblent parfois oublier que le football appartient avant tout à ceux qui le pratiquent et à ceux qui l’aiment. Le véritable problème de Mbappé n’est peut-être pas son football. C’est sa personnalité. Dans un univers où l’on préfère souvent les champions dociles, les ambassadeurs disciplinés et les personnalités façonnées par les stratégies de communication, Mbappé représente une singularité. Il possède une intelligence remarquable, une liberté de parole et une conscience de sa propre valeur. Il ne se contente pas d’être un immense footballeur : il existe également en dehors du terrain. Et c’est précisément cette indépendance qui peut déranger. Le football contemporain n’est plus seulement un sport. Il est devenu une industrie mondiale, un marché de plusieurs milliards, un espace où les grandes puissances financières, les médias et les institutions exercent une influence considérable. Dans cet environnement, les distinctions individuelles peuvent donner le sentiment de répondre à des logiques qui dépassent parfois les seules performances sportives. Le Ballon d’Or conserve son prestige historique. Mais son prestige ne doit pas le placer au-dessus de toute critique. Un jury peut choisir un lauréat. Il ne peut pas décider, à lui seul, de la grandeur d’un joueur. Mbappé n’a pas besoin de l’approbation d’un cercle de décideurs pour démontrer son talent. Ses performances, ses buts et sa capacité à répondre présent dans les grandes confrontations, notamment face au FC Barcelone, constituent une réponse autrement plus éloquente que les discours prononcés dans les salons dorés. Il faut néanmoins distinguer deux mondes : celui du football et celui des affaires du football. Dans le second, Mbappé rencontrera probablement des résistances, des rivalités, des intérêts contradictoires et des batailles d’influence. C’est le prix que paient parfois ceux qui refusent de renoncer à leur indépendance. Mais dans le premier, celui du terrain, des stades et des supporters, sa place est déjà inscrite dans l’histoire. Car les véritables propriétaires émotionnels du football ne sont ni les banques, ni les sponsors, ni les institutions. Ce sont les millions de passionnés qui vibrent devant un exploit, qui se lèvent devant un but et qui transmettent leur admiration d’une génération à l’autre. Kylian, ne laisse jamais le monde des affaires du football te faire douter de ta grandeur dans le monde du football. Tes supporters t’aiment pour ce que tu es, pour ce que tu représentes et pour les émotions que tu leur offres. Ils te suivent aujourd’hui et continueront à te suivre demain. L’histoire du sport nous enseigne une vérité fondamentale : les institutions distribuent les récompenses, mais ce sont les peuples qui consacrent les légendes. Le Ballon d’Or peut couronner un joueur pour une saison. Mais aucun Ballon d’Or ne peut fabriquer une légende, pas plus que son absence ne peut en effacer une. Et Kylian Mbappé appartient déjà à cette catégorie de joueurs dont la grandeur dépasse les cérémonies, les jurys et les calculs. Le football n’a pas besoin d’un Ballon d’Or pour reconnaître Mbappé. C’est peut-être le Ballon d’Or qui a besoin de joueurs comme Mbappé pour préserver sa propre grandeur. The post Mbappé face au Ballon d’Or : quand le génie du football dérange les puissants appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Pakistan, China launch information corridor 'CPIC' to counter misleading narratives, promote cultural exchange
items.description: Pakistan and China have launched the China-Pakistan Information Corridor (CPIC), with Information Minister Ataullah Tarar saying that the initiative will focus on countering misleading narratives, cultural exchanges and cooperation between think tanks. The corridor was launched at a ceremony in Islamabad, which was televised on Tuesday. Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning and Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zaidong attended the launch. In his televised remarks, Tarar expressed his “long-standing“ desire to collaborate with China in the fields of media, information sharing and digital platforms. Hailing Pakistan and China’s bilateral relations, Tarar recalled the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), noting that it had “turned decades of goodwill into steel, concrete and current”. “It lit homes, laid motorways across our provinces and gave Pakistan at Gwadar a gateway to the world.” Tarar said that while the first phase of CPEC connected lands, the next phase will “connect our minds and this information corridor will act as a bridge for connecting the minds of the people of the two countries”. The information minister said the collaboration under the newly launched corridor will stand on four pillars — media, business and enterprises, think tanks, and culture/tourism. “First, media. A news exchange working group of 18 Pakistani and Chinese media organisations. From our state broadcasters and private channels to Xinhua, CMG, and People’s Daily now share verified news on our cooperation.” He added that it will also include a dedicated fact-check mechanism to track misleading narratives and counter them with “concrete facts”. The second pillar, which includes businesses and enterprise, Tarar said, will draw on leading Pakistani and Chinese commercial groups. “This pillar has opened its first regional office in Karachi,” Tarar said, adding that under the initiative, a trade portal to track trade, investment, and Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) was being built, along with a podcast series about the stories of Chinese entrepreneurs in Pakistan and vice versa. He said the third pillar will involve collaboration between think tanks from the two countries. “Led by the Pakistan-China Institute and joined by our foremost research institutions, this pillar will bring evidence and depth to the bilateral conversation through joint dialogue, research, and publications with Chinese counterparts,” Tarar said. The fourth pillar, which Tarar described as the “heart of the corridor”, will focus on tourism, with work already underway on the Xinjiang-Gilgit-Baltistan tourism corridor, “extending the journeys of Chinese travellers into the valleys of our north”. Tarar also shared that the first cohort of CPEC Youth Ambassadors had been nominated from 13 universities across Pakistan. “Before a community of shared future can be built in steel and stone, it must find its place in the minds of the people,” Tarar said, stressing that the principle was at the core of CPIC. “If CPEC is its body and the shared future, CPIC will be its voice. If CPEC connects our economies, CPIC will connect our understanding. Through it, a student in Lahore will know the China of today, and not the caricatures of yesterday. A family in Chengdu will see Pakistan as it truly is: warm, resilient, and full of potential.” He added that the corridor will counter “falsehoods with fact, isolation with exchange, and suspicion with trust,” lauding Chinese President Xi Jinping’s vision. “President Xi gave us the vision of a shared future, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has given Pakistan the means to reach it,” Tarar said. For PM Shehbaz, Tarar said the digital revolution was about people and “above all Pakistan’s young people”. “More than 68 per cent of our nation is under 30 in their hands. A laptop is a passport and a smartphone is a marketplace. Through their talent, Pakistan is taking its place in the global digital economy.” Tarar further stated that CPIC was at its core a “digital corridor”. “Its news exchanges, fact-check mechanisms, trade portals, podcasts, social media channels, and youth ambassadors are tools of a digital age put to work for an old and trusted friendship. And here too, Pakistan walks with China,” Tarar said. The information minister, in his address, also invited Chinese media houses, think tanks, universities, enterprises, and youth ambassadors to join each pillar of CPIC. Concluding his address, Tarar said that while the Karakoram Highway was carved through the mountains, today Pakistan and China were building a “different highway [..] it is not made of rocks, but it is made of truth, and it will be carried not on trucks, but on voices. Meanwhile, China’s Ning also addressed the ceremony, noting that China and Pakistan continue to face misinformation and fake news, according to state broadcaster Pakistan TV. Ning stressed the need for the CPIC, saying that its four pillars can play a key role in highlighting bilateral cooperation. Pakistan and China share a longstanding strategic partnership rooted in mutual trust, economic cooperation and regional connectivity. Over the decades, ties have expanded across different sectors — including trade, energy, defence and infrastructure — with the CPEC symbolising a shared vision for development. A day earlier, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met Ambassador Zaidong to review progress on CPEC. During the meeting in Islamabad, Dar praised the ongoing expansion of the “all-weather strategic cooperative partnership” between the two nations. Discussions focused on advancing trade, investment, regional connectivity, agricultural modernisation and people-to-people exchanges.

items.title: Sousse | Il meurt dans un bar des suites d’une agression violente
items.description: Le ministère public près le Tribunal de première instance de Sousse 2 a ordonné, le week-end dernier, l’ouverture d’une information judiciaire pour homicide volontaire avec préméditation. Cette décision fait suite au signalement du décès d’un homme, âgé d’une soixantaine d’années, dans un bar de la zone d’El-Kantaoui, des suites des blessures infligées lors d’une agression violente. Selon Rafik Boukhama, premier substitut du procureur de la République et porte-parole dudit tribunal, cité par Mosaïque FM , l’enquête a abouti à l’inculpation de deux individus pour meurtre et leur placement en détention par le juge d’instruction auprès dudit tribunal. La mort fait suite à une altercation qui a éclaté entre la victime et un groupe d’individus à l’intérieur du bar et a dégénéré en coups et blessures ayant entraîné la mort de la victime sur place avant l’arrivée des secours. Le différend avait pour objet une jeune femme. I. B. L’article Sousse | Il meurt dans un bar des suites d’une agression violente est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Thiès : Trois ouvriers coincés sous les décombres après l’effondrement d’un bâtiment en construction
items.description: Un bâtiment de type R+5 en construction s’est effondré, ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, à Thiès, à proximité du stade Lat Dior, dans le quartier Sud Stade. Trois ouvriers, dont une fille, sont coincés sous les décombres. La Brigade nationale des sapeurs-pompiers s’est déployée sur les lieux pour tenter de secourir les victimes. Selon les premières informations disponibles, deux d’entre elles présenteraient encore des signes de vie. La Police a également établi un cordon de sécurité autour de la zone pour sécuriser le périmètre et faciliter les opérations de secours. Le gouverneur de la région de Thiès, Saer Ndao, et le préfet du département, Mame Less Cabou, sont sur place pour superviser les opérations. Les circonstances de cet effondrement restent à déterminer. Les opérations de secours se poursuivent pour tenter d’extraire les ouvriers ensevelis sous les décombres. Pour rappel, les services de l'urbanisme avaient servi une sommation d'arrêter les travaux après le constat de dépassement du niveau autorisé de R +3. Mbaye Sarr DIAKHATE (Corespondant)

items.title: Partenariat Afrique-UE : L’Ambassadeur de France sort les chiffres
items.description: Lors d’un entretien accordé à la presse, ce lundi 26 octobre 2026, l’ambassadeur de France en Guinée a apporté des éclaircissements sur le partenariat entre l’Afrique, la France et l’Union européenne. Son objectif : démonter les idées reçues et prouver que l’Europe investit massivement sur le continent, bien plus que tout autre partenaire global. Évoquant cette relation stratégique, Luc Briard a rappelé que l’Union européenne demeure le premier partenaire commercial de l’Afrique. En 2025, les échanges de biens entre les deux régions ont dépassé les 356 milliards de dollars — contre un peu plus de 83 milliards pour les États-Unis. Le diplomate souligne toutefois que ces échanges s'appuient encore sur une structuration traditionnelle des chaînes de valeur, portée par un cadre commercial préférentiel. Résultat : 97 % des exportations africaines à destination de l’UE bénéficient d’une franchise de droits de douane. Abordant le volet des investissements directs étrangers (IDE), l’ambassadeur a rappelé la primauté européenne : avec près de 250 milliards d’euros de stocks d'investissements, l'Europe confirme son ancrage économique majeur. Au-delà du cadre communautaire, la France conserve un poids bilatéral de premier plan, affichant 53 milliards de dollars de stocks d’IDE en 2024 et plus de 400 filiales d’entreprises tricolores implantées sur le continent, générant un demi-million d’emplois. Sur le plan diplomatique, l’UE s'impose comme le principal bailleur de l’Union africaine, avec une aide annuelle moyenne de 260 millions de dollars. Un engagement qui témoigne de la centralité du partenariat entre Bruxelles et l'organisation panafricaine pour le renforcement de ses capacités institutionnelles et opérationnelles. Cette sortie du diplomate français intervient dans un contexte géopolitique brûlant, alors que s'ouvre le Sommet Russie-Afrique. Selon une note interne de l’ambassade de France, consultée par la rédaction de Guineenews , Paris n'hésite pas à pointer l'attitude de Moscou, rappelant que ce partenaire n'apporte aucun soutien financier au budget de l’Union africaine et demeure en marge des opérations de maintien de la paix de l'ONU.

items.description: Le verdict est tombé dans le procès des anciens présidents de la Fédération algérienne de football (FAF). Le pôle pénal économique et financier de Sidi M'hamed (Alger) a condamné ce mardi 27 octobre Kheireddine Zetchi et Amara Charaf-Eddine à 8 ans de prison ferme assortis de 1 millions de dinars d’amende et Djahid Zefizef à 6 ans fermes et une amende du même montant. Les trois hommes se sont succédé à la tête de la Fédération entre 2017 et 2023 (Zetchi 2017-2021, Amara 2021-2022 et Zefizef 2022-2023). Huit ans de prison pour les anciens présidents de la FAF Zetchi et Amara Zetchi et Amara ont écopé des plus lourdes peines. Au total, 19 personnes sont poursuivies dans cette affaire liée à des faits de malversations dans la gestion des deniers de la FAF. Le tribunal a également condamné deux anciens secrétaires généraux de l’instance fédérale, Mohamed Saad et Mounir Debichi, ainsi que l’ancien directeur administratif Abdelghani Nekkache à trois ans de prison ferme, assortis d’une amende de 1 million de dinars chacun. L’ancien manager de l’équipe nationale de football, Amine Abdi, a écopé de la même peine. Les autres peines prononcées à l’encontre du reste des accusés, dont des anciens membres du bureau fédéral, varient entre 1 et 5 ans de prison ferme. items.title: Is There Anything BPC-157 Can’t Cure?
items.description: The wellness industry loves a secret cure. I encountered dozens of them at Dave Asprey’s Beyond Biohacking Conference, held in May on several floors of a hotel in downtown Austin. There were supplements galore, of course: algae tablets for detoxification, ketones for concentration, nitric oxide for circulation. One company claimed that its capsules contained quantum energy. I saw people hooked to IV vitamin drips, sweating inside infrared saunas, and sealed in hyperbaric oxygen chambers. I watched a woman climb into a giant quartz bowl, which someone then struck with a mallet. I tried a pair of inflatable compression pants that rhythmically squeezed my legs to stimulate lymphatic drainage. I also stripped to my boxers and spent a thrillingly miserable two and a half minutes inside a cryotherapy booth. The main attraction, though, was peptides, the short chains of amino acids now hyped as miracle drugs. In a ballroom packed with several hundred people, Asprey and a fellow health guru, Jay Campbell, extolled the many virtues of peptides, railed against restrictions on their promotion, and predicted a future in which they transform mainstream medicine. Both men are in their 50s, with shredded physiques and zero medical degrees. Asprey is best known for popularizing the trend of dumping butter and coconut oil into your coffee. Campbell made his name advocating for testosterone replacement and now bills himself as one of the world’s leading authorities on peptides. He spoke excitedly about one cutting-edge compound, called Klotho, that can “literally lower your biological age.” He told the crowd that he’s heard from women in their 70s who, after taking Klotho and the peptide FLGR242, started menstruating again. (Instead of imploring them to call their doctor, which is what the American Cancer Society recommends for postmenopausal bleeding, his advice was to “keep injecting.”) As peptides become more readily available over the next few years, Campbell anticipates that disease as we know it will come to an end, including “ontological” mutations. (I’m guessing these are mutations that afflict only philosophers.) Campbell and Asprey have been promoting underground peptides in their books and on their podcasts for years. Lately, though, these gray-market drugs have started to gain traction with a broader audience. The most talked-about among them goes by the cryptic designation BPC‑157. It’s commonplace enough that asking questions about it immediately tags you as a tourist. BPC‑157 is a component in most of the popular peptide combos, ones with names such as Glow, Klow, and Wolverine (a reference to the comic-book superhero with self-healing powers, not the carcass-eating skunk-bear). It’s rumored to be good for stomach ailments including acid reflux, bloating, and ulcers. Also, sprained ankles. It will reportedly ameliorate arthritis, carpal tunnel syndrome, and sciatica, not to mention hernias and migraines. BPC‑157 has been said to loosen stiff shoulders and repair runner’s knee. Suffering from bursitis? Gingivitis? Road rash? Low libido? Its boosters promise that it can help with all of these conditions and more. In recent months, BPC‑157’s profile has risen significantly, at least judging by Google searches and Instagram videos, some of which feature a creepy AI-generated character who magically restores torn ligaments. Praise from big-name podcasters such as Andrew Huberman and Joe Rogan has no doubt contributed to its popularity (Rogan declared BPC‑157 “super legit”). Reliable sales figures, though, are hard to come by. Conventional drugs that have been approved by the FDA—including GLP-1s like Ozempic, which are also peptides—are sold by multibillion-dollar global behemoths with legions of researchers and executives. Peptides like BPC‑157 are sold by … honestly, who knows? The companies pop up and disappear. The proprietor of your favorite American peptide supplier might be an enterprising undergraduate who buys in bulk from China, where many peptides are manufactured, and relabels them. A small glass vial of freeze-dried powder arrives on your doorstep; you dissolve the powder in sterile water, draw it into a syringe, and inject it into your abdomen. Peptides are usually advertised as “for research use only,” a wink-wink disclaimer that allows vendors to maintain that they’re not violating federal laws regulating drug sales. Maybe that gives you pause. Or maybe you think that these sketchy transactions are necessary because the establishment—that is, Big Pharma and the United States government—is suppressing the good stuff. Amid the sellers of red-light panels and blue-light glasses at Beyond, I stumbled on a company marketing a drinkable version of BPC‑157. Its giveaway sticker read We Prefer Oral Peptides , with the word peptides in much smaller letters because haha sex. The representative behind the counter referred to BPC‑157 as “the soccer mom’s peptide” and nonchalantly squirted some from what was essentially a hand-soap dispenser into a tiny plastic cup, then held it out to me. I hesitated, and the peptide hung in the air, unclaimed. “Are you afraid of it?” he asked. The not-so-subtle subtext was that I shouldn’t be, that taking BPC‑157 was equivalent to trying the dissolvable herbal-tea strips a few tables down or giving the giant quartz bowl a whirl. For the record: We were in a hotel hallway and I was being encouraged—dared, really—to try a drug that isn’t FDA-approved, is prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency for athletes’ use, and allegedly works throughout the body via some mysterious mechanism that is not entirely predictable. I was being offered an unspecified dose, although I wouldn’t know what dose would be appropriate, because there are no agreed-upon dosing guidelines. I declined the peptide. The representative shrugged and drank it himself. Perhaps I was being too cautious. Thousands of Americans have ingested or injected BPC‑157. That guy didn’t keel over after he swigged it. Whatever you think of their relevant credentials, Asprey and Campbell appear to be insufferably healthy middle-aged men. Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the secretary of health and human services, is on record as being “ a big fan of peptides ,” a casually sweeping endorsement of an entire class of drugs. Although Kennedy has stoked vaccine hesitancy for most of this century and argues that Americans are overmedicated, he has a soft spot for these particular shots. The “Make America Healthy Again” movement is officially on board too, which feels strange considering that MAHA is all about treating anything modern and artificial with suspicion. They’re the raw-milk people! They don’t even like Doritos and Coca-Cola! And yet they’ve decided that these highly processed powders, assembled by machines that link amino acids together, are somehow consistent with the nature-knows-best ethos. For MAHA, the renegade cachet of peptides is central to their appeal, and the fact that medical experts are wary of them is a plus. Under Kennedy, the FDA may soon allow six peptides, including BPC‑157, to be made in the United States, which would mean that doctors could prescribe them, and that telehealth companies such as Hims & Hers, best known for discreetly shipping men generic Viagra, could offer them for sale. [ Read: America is about to go over a peptide cliff ] Is there any evidence that BPC‑157 works? Its evangelists like to note that the peptide has several decades of peer-reviewed research behind it. Those papers, more than 200 of them, are packed with charts and citations and have been published in journals that are respectable enough, if not quite top-tier. BPC‑157 has been tested on mice, rabbits, guinea pigs, chickens, honeybees, and, above all else, rats. So many rats. These rats have endured all manner of miseries in the name of science. They have had their tendons severed, stomachs ulcerated, tails amputated, muscles crushed, bowels perforated, spinal cords compressed, blood vessels tied off. The ones that received the peptide consistently fared better, according to the studies: Their wounds closed more quickly, tendons knitted together more completely, ulcers shrank. Overall, they were more likely to survive this catalog of laboratory horrors than the unlucky controls. If the published literature is to be believed, BPC‑157 is a rodent panacea. When you read the papers, one after another, until you’re bleary-eyed and bewildered, you start to notice some patterns. One is that very few of these studies have been conducted on humans, and humans, famously, are not rats. Another is that, as I’ve already suggested, BPC‑157 is said to work almost every time for almost everything. Behold these triumphant verbs: improves , enhances , promotes , stimulates , accelerates , restores , increases , prevents , abolishes , counteracts , heals , protects . And it seems to yield benefits regardless of the form, or method of application, or which orifice it is delivered into. Also, when you examine the list of authors, you see many of the same names crop up again and again. One name, however, appears at the top of nearly every paper: Predrag Sikirić. Sikirić is a 72-year-old professor emeritus of pharmacology at the University of Zagreb School of Medicine, in Croatia. I emailed him. I wanted to know where this wondrous elixir, supposedly good for both heartburn and a ruptured Achilles, came from, and why we’re hearing about it only from podcasters. Precisely four minutes later, my phone buzzed. An insistent man with a thick accent wanted to know how quickly I could get on a plane. The current global hub for BPC‑157 research is a cramped, cluttered room with a single window half-obscured by a tangle of plants. Sikirić’s laboratory is at the university’s medical school, roughly a mile north of Zagreb’s main square, near a small café where future doctors smoke cigarettes and grouse about their workload. These modest quarters are temporary; renovations are under way on a larger laboratory in the building across the street. For now, new experiments are on hold, and Sikirić and his longtime lab assistant are confined to a glorified storage closet with empty rat enclosures stacked next to boxes of small plastic tubes and bags of feed. Among the haphazard decorations—including a foam brain and a hat that reads HAPPY ANIMAL HAPPY HUMAN —hangs a collage of patent medicines from the heyday of cure-alls, back when you could make whatever claims you wished about your restorative tonic without fear of government regulators shutting you down. On a counter sits a large glass bottle of clear liquid, the letters BPC scrawled on the label in blue marker. The peptide in that bottle is Sikirić’s life’s work. When he was still a student, inspired by the pioneering research of the endocrinologist Hans Selye, who studied the biological effects of stress , Sikirić came to believe that the body produced, in essence, some universal antidote to injury, a molecule that would cue damaged tissue to return to its normal state, regardless of what had caused the harm. He reasoned that the remedy was probably found in gastric juice, because the stomach is constantly adjusting to fresh insults. Sikirić spent the 1980s searching for it, and the decades since trying to convince the world that he found it. Along the way, his work has often drawn eye rolls from colleagues at the medical school, some of whom remain unmoved by the animal evidence he has amassed. Even those who admire Sikirić’s persistence and have known him for years, such as Miloš Judaš, the director of the university’s Croatian Institute for Brain Research, do not share his faith in the curative properties of BPC‑157 (“We are not sure whether it really works or not,” Judaš told me). Sikirić’s discussions with pharmaceutical companies have repeatedly stalled. The recognition he believed would be forthcoming from the scientific community has never materialized, despite his prolific scholarly output. But none of that has deterred Sikirić in his effort to, as he told me, “bring BPC to mankind.” He’s just kept plugging away at this singular line of research, coaxing generations of graduate students to join him in the mission, and dreaming up new experiments to test his theory. Now the world is seeking him out. Along with reporters like me, he hears from peptide promoters eager to brag about being buddies with the discoverer of BPC‑157. How his peptide took center stage, Sikirić isn’t sure. For a long time, BPC‑157 wasn’t really known outside his lab except among readers of niche scientific journals such as Digestive Diseases and Sciences and the European Journal of Pharmacology . In the mid-2010s, it began appearing on bodybuilding forums and in biohacking guides, where it was touted as a way to speed healing and recovery. But it remained on the fringes until recently. Testimonials from Rogan and Huberman, whose health recommendations reach enormous audiences, certainly helped spread the word: Rogan swore it fixed his hurt elbow, while Huberman credited it with eliminating his back pain. Mare Milin for The Atlantic Predrag Sikirić has published hundreds of papers purporting to show the salutary effects of the peptide BPC⁠-157. However it happened, Sikirić is pleased that his peptide is at last having its moment. He is gratified that BPC‑157 is flourishing on the gray market as well. “Officially, I have to be against any kind of usage without full approval,” he said. Unofficially, he’s all for it. He interprets BPC‑157’s word-of-mouth success as proof that his peptide is helping the masses. If it wasn’t, why would so many people recommend it? He is delighted, too, that the health secretary of the United States is a believer in peptides. I asked if he’s ever spoken with Kennedy, who has a habit of reaching out to researchers whose work he admires. “I would kindly reject to reply to the question,” he said. “This is good English?” (An HHS spokesperson did not respond to an inquiry about whether Kennedy had spoken with Sikirić.) Sikirić can be at once engaging and cagey. Try to pin him down, and he launches into an unrelated anecdote. Broach a contentious topic, and he responds with a puzzling analogy. Ask about his past, and he grudgingly provides a few biographical details. Sikirić grew up in Zagreb, which was then part of Yugoslavia. His father, a lawyer, was jailed repeatedly for his opposition to the country’s ruling Communist party; his mother, an encyclopedia editor, encountered government censorship. As a child, Sikirić underwent multiple surgeries, and those hospital stays made him want to be a doctor. Medicine also offered an escape from politics: “The pain is the pain for anybody,” he said. After medical school, he worked for three years as an emergency physician in a small town, treating victims of car accidents, heart attacks, and stabbings. But a country doctor can only do so much. The wonder drug he envisioned might help millions. Sikirić returned to the University of Zagreb to pursue this dream with a single-minded, near-manic intensity. In addition to churning out hundreds of papers, he has supervised numerous doctoral dissertations, all of them on BPC‑157. His students tell of late-night phone calls from Sikirić, eager to share an insight. He and his wife of more than 40 years don’t have children. He has no hobbies, doesn’t take vacations to the nearby coast, and works for long stretches without a break. Sikirić walks quickly, albeit at a slight angle, as if he might tip over. He drives quickly, too: When I rode with him, he sped through downtown Zagreb, braking a few feet from crossing pedestrians, half-grinning at my evident anxiety. You wouldn’t think it to look at him—baggy professorial sweater and corduroys, tightly cropped gray hair—but Sikirić is a septuagenarian in a hurry. BPC‑157’s newfound fame has brought with it unwelcome scrutiny. Last year, a group of researchers in Poland raised concerns about BPC‑157’s safety, arguing that how it works is poorly understood and warning that it could cause neurological damage or promote tumor growth. These possibilities, they wrote, must be considered “before falling into complete admiration.” In response, Sikirić pointed to his animal studies suggesting that BPC‑157, on the contrary, inhibits tumor growth and protects against neurological damage. When I asked him about the Polish paper, he dismissed it as a bid for attention and emphasized how much it upset him. If BPC‑157 really increased the risk of cancer, Sikirić insists that he would tell the public to stop using it immediately. One argument for BPC‑157’s safety rests on the assumption that if the body makes it, it must be safe. But does the body make it? Sikirić has asserted that his peptide is a fragment of a protein, but he’s never publicly shared key details about that protein. Several researchers have attempted to locate BPC-157’s amino-acid sequence in databases of protein and DNA sequences, to no avail. I asked William Pearson, a computational biologist who co-developed the first widely used search tool for such databases, to try to determine where BPC‑157 comes from. After hours of combing through repositories containing hundreds of millions of protein and DNA sequences, Pearson couldn’t find a match. If the peptide occurs in humans, those searches should have turned it up. He also identified no matches among proteins from other animals—including, it’s worth noting, rats. Sikirić downplayed the failed searches. He doubts that those databases are comprehensive, though he acknowledged that he hasn’t used them himself. Sikirić told me he’s sure that BPC‑157 originates in humans because he isolated it from newborns in the ’90s. I didn’t remember seeing that study in any of his papers, but that’s because Sikirić says he never published it and doesn’t intend to (“Some things you have to keep for yourself,” he said). As for the gene behind BPC‑157, he maintains that he’s close to finding it, but won’t reveal how he is conducting that search. He likened providing such basic information to a country disclosing its nuclear secrets. The answers, he said, could be found only in his head. I asked what would happen if he got run over by a bus: “This could be huge problem.” Sikirić believes that, like the cure-alls in his office collage, his peptide can be applied to any ailment, from minor aches to major diseases. During my stay in Zagreb, we played a little game: I named a malady and he told me whether BPC‑157 could treat it. Macular degeneration? “Yes, it could.” Gut inflammation? “This is the favorite site of activity.” Dementia? “Certainly.” COVID? “Naturally, yes.” Concussions? “We published data about it.” Anxiety? “The experiment was helpful in the mice.” Depression? “Exactly.” Heart attacks? “Any kind of condition.” Headaches? “Any kind of pain.” In Sikirić’s estimation, BPC‑157 can do no wrong. Its all-purpose goodness is fundamental to his theory: The peptide is consistently returning the body to its healthiest state. Other drugs have limitations and downsides, but not BPC‑157. He compares it to steroids, but believes it’s superior because BPC‑157 has no known toxic dose (“You could eat BPC without any harm—literally eat, like bread,” he said) and you can take it indefinitely. Until I told him, Sikirić seemed unaware that some users report distressing side effects from BPC‑157. There’s an online support group called “Haters of BPC‑157,” in which people who believe that the peptide has harmed them commiserate and trade notes on recovery. The most common complaint appears to be anhedonia, which is a kind of emotional numbing. They say they struggle to feel pleasure after taking the peptide. Some blame themselves for using an unapproved drug. Others are angry at Sikirić (“Fuck him,” one member of the group messaged me). Sikirić told me he felt sorry that people were suffering but doesn’t believe it has anything to do with his peptide. (Predictably, he contends that BPC‑157 actually counteracts anhedonia.) Maybe the product they bought was contaminated, he argued, or maybe the cause was something else entirely. These are only anecdotes, he pointed out. And he’s right; that is all they are. But the human evidence in favor of BPC‑157 is also largely anecdotal. Illustration by The Atlantic . Sources: Durham Peptides; Ultra Pure Bioscience; Amino Research; XL Peptides. Peptides are usually listed as “for research use only,” a disclaimer to skirt federal laws regulating drug sales. Sikirić takes BPC‑157 himself. Of course he does. I first suspected this when I noticed an empty plastic tube in the cup holder in his car. He was somewhat sheepish when I asked about it, and not forthcoming about how often, or for what purpose, he takes it. As a rule, it’s frowned upon for scientists to sample the merchandise, though there have been famous exceptions. Jonas Salk tested the polio vaccine on himself before it was given to millions of American children; Albert Hofmann dropped way too much acid once before biking home. I asked many of Sikirić’s colleagues and former students if they had taken BPC‑157. Several told me they would never try a drug that hadn’t been approved for human use. Others swore by it. They use it when they feel a cold coming on. They blend it into a cream and smear it on burns and diaper rash. They take it when they twist their ankle or strain their back. A bunch of them give it to their dogs. One former student, now a doctor, showed me a small tube of BPC‑157 that she carries in her purse, just in case. This is not how drug development is supposed to work. After a promising candidate is tested on animals, it normally passes through three phases of human clinical trials, after which regulators review the evidence and make a determination. The story of why BPC‑157 hasn’t followed this path is convoluted. More than two decades ago, clinical trials began under the auspices of Pliva, a Croatian drug company, but didn’t reach the third phase. Pliva’s research institute, which was responsible for new drug development, was acquired by GlaxoSmithKline in 2006, and progress on BPC‑157 subsequently ceased. In Sikirić’s version, GSK, as it’s now known, decided to shelve the peptide because it was too effective and the company feared it would cannibalize sales of its other drugs. “Let’s just say major breakthroughs are not welcome,” he told me. Yet it’s hard to imagine a pharmaceutical company nixing an important discovery knowing that a competitor might snatch it up. A study conducted by Pliva researchers found that although BPC‑157 did hasten the healing of skin wounds in rats, the results were similar to those achieved with an already approved drug. The peptide did something, in other words, but it wasn’t a breakthrough. Another problem may have been Sikirić himself. Two former Pliva employees involved in the BPC‑157 project told me Sikirić’s passion sometimes seemed to override his objectivity. He bristled at pushback, and his commitment bordered on obsession. As one of them put it, when it came to his peptide, “Predrag was in love.” Neither knew for sure why GSK didn’t move forward with BPC‑157 (a GSK spokesperson told me she couldn’t find anyone with knowledge about a decision made 20 years ago). But they noted that it’s far from unusual for experimental drugs to be abandoned during clinical trials; in fact, about 90 percent don’t make it all the way through the process, including ones that show some benefit in animal studies. After GSK dropped the peptide, the rights were returned to Sikirić, allowing him to pursue BPC‑157 trials elsewhere. In 2015, a Phase 1 clinical trial was conducted in Tijuana, Mexico, but the results have never been published. The trial’s sponsor was PharmaCotherapia, a Croatian company co-owned by Sikirić that last year reported having no employees. Sikirić let me briefly review the safety findings on his laptop but declined to share the full report. The summary I read described mild adverse events among some subjects but concluded that BPC‑157 was “safe and well tolerated.” According to Sikirić, the report was never published because the trial’s principal investigator, Rufino Menchaca, a clinical neurologist, wouldn’t sign off once the trial was completed (Menchaca, through a representative, declined to speak with me). The reason for his refusal to sign isn’t entirely clear, although Sikirić told me it had to do with worry that others would steal the data if they were published. Sikirić hopes to restart clinical trials soon, again in Tijuana, looking specifically at whether BPC‑157 is a beneficial treatment for multiple sclerosis—though, in his mind, there is no question. He’s certain that the experiments will confirm his expectations. Sikirić is so determined to vindicate BPC‑157 that he frequently sounds more like a salesman than a scientist. Money, however, doesn’t seem to be what drives him: As Sikirić will admit, he has no knack for business, and at the moment it’s shady online sellers who are getting rich from his peptide, not him. He just wants to be right, and he wouldn’t mind getting some credit, too. As I’m typing this, Sikirić is sending me yet more papers via WhatsApp even though it’s after midnight in Croatia. He needs me, and everyone else, to set aside any misgivings and agree with him that BPC‑157 is a marvel. Skepticism is taken as an insult. Too often Sikirić’s message is: Trust me . Trust me about where BPC‑157 comes from. Trust me that it works on humans, not just rats. Trust me that it’s safe. FDA scientists don’t seem to trust him. In June, the FDA published a 68-page report that looked closely at BPC‑157 studies and found them unconvincing, arguing that they lack sufficient human-safety data and that too little is known about how or whether the peptide works. Agency researchers couldn’t tell from the literature how dosage affected outcomes. They flagged the possibility that it could provoke harmful immune-system reactions. Claims about BPC‑157 should be “interpreted with caution,” they wrote, because of troubling gaps in the literature. But when an FDA advisory committee met in July, it more or less disregarded that report and recommended allowing BPC‑157 , along with five other peptides, to be made by licensed compounding pharmacies in the United States. It probably wasn’t a coincidence that weeks before the vote, the agency had announced the appointments of eight new committee members , six of whom had ties to the wellness industry, which hopes to capitalize on a regulatory change. (An HHS spokesperson told me that “all committee members underwent the same ethics review and vetting process required of all FDA advisory committee members.”) One peptide lobbyist told me that the projected profits for BPC‑157 could be in the billions. Hims & Hers plans to start manufacturing BPC‑157 and allowing customers with a prescription to purchase it, assuming the FDA gives the green light (the company’s CEO, Andrew Dudum, told shareholders that he was “extremely excited about this category”). Although FDA officials still have to accept the committee’s recommendation, that seems like a formality, given that Kennedy oversees the agency. [ Read: The peptide boom is getting out of hand ] I have mixed feelings about the move. No, we don’t know enough about these peptides, and providing what amounts to backdoor government approval seems like a terrible idea. At the same time, if people are going to take BPC‑157, I’d rather the supply come from a licensed pharmacy than some guy with a storage unit and an overseas hookup. I kept thinking about the question the peptide representative at the Beyond conference asked me: “Are you afraid of it?” Sikirić sent me home with a small plastic tube containing a single milligram of BPC‑157. It looked like nothing, barely a few grains of fine white powder. I considered taking it, both for the sake of this story and because I have this weird twinge in my right shoulder sometimes. Instead, I sent it off to get tested. The report that came back was glowing: Unlike the gray-market peptides, many of which contain filler and God knows what else, the peptide from Sikirić’s laboratory was chemically pure, full-strength, 100 percent BPC‑157. It was the real thing—whatever that is. This article appears in the December 2026 print edition with the headline “Mr. Peptide.”

items.title: Indian court orders takedown of documentary on billionaire Gautam Adani, PM Modi
items.description: An Indian court has ordered the takedown of an online documentary posted by Hotmail co-founder Sabeer Bhatia accusing Prime ​Minister Narendra Modi and billionaire Gautam Adani of cronyism, after Adani Enterprises sued, calling it defamatory. Adani’s flagship firm, Adani ‌Enterprises, told the high court in the eastern city of Kolkata that the documentary, which garnered millions of views on social media in recent days, was riddled with false content and had prompted inquiries from some investors in the company, whom the court order did not name. The documentary “is not a news report or an ​account of proceedings. It is a dramatised narrative,” the court’s takedown order for YouTube, X and Meta issued late on Monday ​said. Adani Enterprises, Modi’s office and Bhatia did not respond to requests for comment, and neither did the social ⁠media companies. Modi’s opponents have often accused the prime minister of having close ties with Adani, saying the business tycoon has received favourable ​treatment over the years. The Indian government and the Adani group have repeatedly denied those allegations. In its challenge, Adani Enterprises told the court ​that it does not seek to restrain constructive criticism of government policy or of business concentration, but Bhatia had suppressed material facts, according to the court order. Bhatia, who is based in the US, wrote on his X account that the lawsuit demands 500 million rupees ($5.25 million) in damages. In one X post, he wrote: “Truth ​is on my side”. “I believe the documentary has rattled Adani Enterprises Limited and struck a nerve at the highest levels,” he wrote. Bhatia is ​the co-founder of the once-popular email service Hotmail, which he sold to Microsoft in 1997. Order to take down In an interim order in force until January 31, 2027, the ‌court ordered ⁠YouTube, X and Meta’s Instagram to remove several posts of the 36-minute film, “The Friendship Files”. It also restrained Bhatia from disseminating the video. Hearings in the case are likely to resume in January. Ahead of the court challenge, police in the state of Maharashtra, which is led by Modi’s ruling alliance, sent a takedown notice to Bhatia on October 19, saying the content “made serious unsubstantiated allegations”. Modi’s political opponents have repeatedly been sharing the ​documentary, saying it reflected similar ​allegations they had made about the ⁠two men. The film used archival footage to trace the history of the relationship between Modi and Adani, starting in the western state of Gujarat, where both men come from. It raised questions about Adani’s winning ​bid for six airports in 2019 after a government rule change that critics say favoured his enterprise — allegations ​similar to those ⁠levelled by the opposition Congress party. The Adani group has denied such allegations and the government says all regulations were complied with and there is no favouritism. Earlier, regional opposition leader and Modi critic Raj Thackeray shared the documentary on his X account, where it garnered 4.8 million views, but took ⁠it down, ​saying he was doing it at the request of the Mumbai police commissioner. Mahua Moitra, ​another political opponent of Modi and a lawmaker, posted the documentary on October 11 and said it was still online. “I posted this on Oct 11th. It is still ​on my timeline, so do watch it,” she wrote on X on Monday night.

items.title: FC Ashantigold 04 dismisses head coach Karim Zito
items.description: FC Ashantigold 04 have dismissed head coach Abdul Karim Zito, assistant coach Ernest Okyere and goalkeeper’s trainer Robert Dabo with immediate effect. The Obuasi-based club announced the decision in a statement on Tuesday, October 27, following a consultative meeting by the Interim Management Committee. The club added that a caretaker coach would take charge of the team until a substantive head coach and technical director is appointed. “Subsequently, a caretaker Coach has been appointed to steer the affairs of the team until the appointment of a substantive Coach/Technical Director. “Management wishes to express our deepest gratitude to the affected officials for their contribution and service to the team thus far, and wishes them the best in their subsequent endeavours.” Zito joined the Division One League side in February 2026, 15 days after resigning from Asante Kotoko, where he had been in charge at the time. The former Dreams FC coach subsequently guided Ashantigold to promotion to the Ghana Premier League. However, the club have endured a mixed start to the 2026/27 campaign, recording three wins, three defeats and two draws in their opening eight matches. Ashantigold currently sit 11th on the league table with 11 points.

items.description: El yemení Yassen S.A solicitó protección internacional en Ceuta y su petición fue rechazada. Su abogada recurrió, y la Sala de lo Contencioso Administrativo de la Audiencia Nacional le concedió este lunes una medida cautelarísima, algo que le permitía permanecer en territorio español mientras se resolvía su recurso y que evitaba que ejecutaran su devolución. A pesar de eso, fue detenido en el Centro Temporal de Estancia de Inmigrantes (CETI) de la ciudad y devuelto a Marruecos el mismo lunes, como ha adelantado la Cadena SER. En los últimos días se han producido algunos casos como el de Yassen S.A., según denuncian varias asociaciones humanitarias. Una de ellas cita dos casos, del pasado viernes, en los que los migrantes ―procedentes de Yemen y Bangladesh― también contaban con medidas cautelarísimas que no se respetaron. Seguir leyendo

items.title: LFR 2026 : Ces éventuelles conséquences d’un rejet parlementaire
items.description: Un rejet de la loi de finances rectificative (LFR) par l’Assemblée nationale pourrait avoir des conséquences à la fois budgétaires, économiques et politiques. Le rejet de la loi de finances rectificative (LFR), ce 27 octobre, entrainerait pour le Gouvernement une marge de manœuvre budgétaire réduite pour l’exercice 2026. Le Gouvernement se verrait priver de l’autorisation parlementaire nécessaire, à la mise en œuvre des modifications proposées. Il devrait alors continuer à s’appuyer sur les crédits et les autorisations budgétaires en vigueur, dans les limites prévues, par les textes applicables. Des risques pour la trésorerie des entreprises et l’exécution des investissements C’est probablement l’un des enjeux économiques les plus immédiats, compte tenu des arguments avancés par le Gouvernement lors de sa conférence de presse du 25 octobre 2026. Le Premier ministre, Ahmadou Al Aminou Mohamed Lo rappelait lors de cette conférence de presse « si la LFR n’est pas votée, des entreprises du BTP, les fournisseurs de l’État et les prestataires publics pourraient notamment subir les effets d’un éventuel report des paiements ou de la reprise de certains chantiers ». Les conséquences pourraient se répercuter sur les sous-traitants, l’emploi et les revenus des ménages. L’impact dépendrait cependant des crédits déjà disponibles, des engagements existants et des dispositions précises du projet rejeté. Un bras de fer institutionnel et un risque pour la crédibilité financière du Sénégal Un blocage pourrait susciter des interrogations chez les partenaires financiers et les investisseurs. Une telle crise de confiance est susceptible de fragiliser la stratégie économique gouvernementale, si elle se prolonge sans compromis. Cependant, le rejet intervenu en commission des Finances ne vaut pas rejet définitif du projet. Le texte doit encore être examiné en séance plénière, ce 27 octobre. L’enjeu se situe sur la posture adoptée par les députés. Il s’agira de voir s’ils rejettent définitivement le texte ou s’ils chercheront à en modifier les arbitrages. L’article 86, alinéa 6, de la Constitution cet autre mécanisme d’arbitrage L’article 86, alinéa 6, de la Constitution sénégalaise permet au Premier ministre, après délibération du Conseil des ministres, d’engager la responsabilité du Gouvernement devant l’Assemblée nationale sur le vote d’un projet de loi de finances. Le texte est alors considéré comme adopté, sauf si une motion de censure est déposée, dans les 24 heures puis votée dans les conditions constitutionnelles prévues. Les spécialistes du droit public sont cependant partagés sur la question. D’aucuns jugent cette interprétation extensive. En pratique, si cette procédure était jugée applicable, elle permettrait au Gouvernement de faire adopter le projet, sans obtenir un vote favorable des députés. En contrepartie, elle l’exposerait au risque, d’une motion de censure. O.BA

items.title: Un suspect arrêté après huit mois de cavale
items.description: La Brigade de recherches de Dakar a interpellé, le 25 octobre 2026, un individu recherché depuis février et visé par un mandat d’arrêt international. Selon la Gendarmerie nationale, il est concerné par plusieurs affaires présumées, dont un dossier foncier de plus de 1,372 milliard de F CFA et une enquête sur une fraude présumée de 300 millions de F CFA liée à des comptes de monnaie électronique. Huit mois après le début de sa cavale, un individu recherché par la justice a été arrêté aux Almadies, à Dakar. L’interpellation a eu lieu, le dimanche 25 octobre 2026, dans un appartement, au terme de plusieurs mois de fuite, selon la Gendarmerie nationale. Le suspect est notamment poursuivi dans une première affaire pour évasion, association de malfaiteurs, escroquerie, faux et usage de faux et blanchiment de capitaux. Durant sa fuite, il aurait séjourné successivement au Maroc, en Côte d’Ivoire, en Guinée et en Gambie, avant de regagner le Sénégal. Son arrestation intervient également dans le cadre d’une enquête sur une fraude présumée de 300 millions de F CFA impliquant des comptes de monnaie électronique Wave et Orange Money. À cela, s’ajoute un dossier foncier portant sur un montant supérieur à 1,372 milliard de F CFA. Les enquêteurs poursuivent leurs investigations afin de faire la lumière sur ces différentes affaires, d’établir les responsabilités et de déterminer l’éventuelle implication de complices. Le matériel saisi au domicile du suspect doit également être exploité dans le cadre de la procédure. L’enquête se poursuit pour déterminer les circonstances exactes des faits présumés et établir les responsabilités éventuelles, dans le respect de la présomption d’innocence. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Un suspect arrêté après huit mois de cavale est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .
